determination:
FINAL DISPOSITION: REMAND

HEALTHFIRST APPEALS AND GRIEVANCES DEPARTMENT
P.O. Box 9000
San Francisco, CA 94120

Date: October 24, 2024

CASE ID: PA-2024-D001
MEMBER NAME: Sandra White
MEMBER ID: M-334466
PLAN: HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
STATE OF RESIDENCE: California
REQUESTING PROVIDER: Dr. Paul Lee, MD — Neurosurgery
FACILITY: UCLA Medical Center
PROCEDURE REQUESTED: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C6-C7, one level (CPT 22551)
ORIGINAL DENIAL DATE: October 5, 2024
ORIGINAL REVIEWER: Dr. Alan Foster, MD

APPEAL DETERMINATION: REMAND

Dear Ms. White and Dr. Lee,

The HealthFirst Appeals and Grievances Department has completed its review of the first-level appeal submitted on October 18, 2024, regarding the prior authorization denial for the requested anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at C6-C7 (CPT 22551). 

After a comprehensive review of the clinical documentation, the plan's clinical coverage criteria, and the California regulatory framework, the final disposition of this appeal is a REMAND. The plan is directed to immediately vacate the defective denial notice dated October 5, 2024, and reissue a legally compliant notice that specifies the exact clinical criteria applied and includes the mandatory Independent Medical Review (IMR) notice as required by California law.

Below is a detailed analysis of the clinical and regulatory findings that support this determination.

I. CLINICAL BACKGROUND AND PRESENTING PRESENTATION
The clinical record indicates that Ms. Sandra White is a 44-year-old female with a primary presenting diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy at C6-C7.
- Imaging: An MRI of the cervical spine dated August 15, 2024, demonstrated a C6-C7 disc herniation with moderate right C7 nerve root compression. The MRI showed no spinal cord contact and no evidence of myelomalacia (cord signal change).
- Neurological Examination: A physical examination performed by Dr. Paul Lee on August 20, 2024, revealed objective neurological deficits, including right C7 dermatomal numbness, tricep weakness graded at 4/5 on the right, and a diminished right tricep reflex.
- Conservative Treatment:
  - Physical Therapy: Ms. White completed 4 weeks of supervised physical therapy (total of 12 sessions). While the member reported reaching a functional plateau, the physical therapy discharge summary did not explicitly document a functional plateau.
  - Pharmacotherapy: Ms. White trialed one pharmacological agent, Ibuprofen 800mg TID, for a duration of 6 weeks, which provided only partial relief.
  - Interventional Treatment: No interventional treatments (such as cervical epidural steroid injections, medial branch blocks, or trigger point injections) have been performed.

II. SUBSTANTIVE CLINICAL REVIEW (PLAN CRITERIA CC-SPINE-2024)
Under HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria document CC-SPINE-2024 (Effective January 1, 2024), Section 2.2 outlines the conservative treatment requirements that must be satisfied prior to surgical authorization for CPT 22551:

1. Physical Therapy (Section 2.2(a)): Requires a minimum of 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy with documented functional outcomes. Ms. White completed only 4 weeks of physical therapy, representing a 2-week shortfall.
2. Pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)): Requires a trial of at least two specified agents (NSAIDs, muscle relaxants, neuropathic agents, or oral corticosteroids) for a minimum of 4 weeks each. Ms. White trialed only one agent (Ibuprofen) for 6 weeks, representing a shortfall of one pharmacological agent trial.
3. Interventional Treatment (Section 2.2(c)): Requires at least one interventional treatment, such as a cervical epidural steroid injection, medial branch block, or trigger point injection series. Ms. White has had no interventional treatments, representing a complete shortfall of this requirement.

Exception 2.2(A) (Myelopathy Pathway):
The clinical record does not support the application of the Myelopathy Pathway exception. Under CC-SPINE-2024, this exception reduces the physical therapy requirement to 4 weeks and waives the interventional treatment requirement, but it "applies only when myelopathy is the PRIMARY diagnosis." Ms. White's primary diagnosis is cervical radiculopathy. Furthermore, her MRI dated August 15, 2024, explicitly notes "no cord contact" and "no myelomalacia," which are required clinical indicators for cervical myelopathy under Section 2.1(b) and DMHC All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014.

Therefore, on the substantive clinical merits, the clinical record does not satisfy the plan's internal coverage criteria for surgical intervention at this time.

III. PROCEDURAL REGULATORY REVIEW (CALIFORNIA LAW)
While the clinical criteria were not met, the original denial notice issued by HealthFirst on October 5, 2024, contains critical procedural defects under California law that invalidate the denial:

1. Failure to Specify Clinical Criteria (CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2)):
California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(a)(2) mandates that when a health plan issues a denial based on medical necessity, the written notice must include "the specific criteria applied" and "the specific clinical reason for the denial." The denial notice dated October 5, 2024, contained only a generic reference to plan criteria, failing to cite the specific document (CC-SPINE-2024), the relevant section (Section 2.2), or the specific criteria that failed.

2. Failure to Include Independent Medical Review (IMR) Notice (CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2)):
CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2) requires health plans to include a notice of the member's right to an Independent Medical Review (IMR) in all medical necessity denial notices. The plan's original denial notice failed to include this mandatory IMR notice.

Under CHSC § 1374.31(b), "A denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason for the denial is DEFECTIVE and shall be treated as if no denial was issued for purposes of appeal timelines."

3. Mechanical Application of Physical Therapy Requirements (CIC § 10169.5):
California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(c) states that a plan's internal requirement for a minimum number of weeks of physical therapy shall not be applied mechanically without reference to whether the member has achieved a functional plateau or whether the condition involves neurological urgency. Although the clinical record lacks the required pharmacotherapy and interventional trials, the plan's mechanical denial based on the 4-week physical therapy duration, without evaluating the member's reported functional plateau or the objective neurological deficits (4/5 tricep weakness), constitutes a major regulatory non-compliance under CIC § 10169.5.

IV. RESOLUTION OF CONFLICT AND REMEDY
In resolving the conflict between the member's clinical non-compliance and the plan's procedural violations, California regulatory authority takes absolute precedence over internal plan guidelines. 

Because the denial notice dated October 5, 2024, is procedurally defective under CHSC § 1374.31(b), it cannot stand. However, because the clinical record does not currently support the medical necessity of the surgical procedure under either the plan's criteria (CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2) or generally accepted clinical standards (which require a full course of conservative treatment for non-urgent cervical radiculopathy), an outright overturn of the denial is clinically inappropriate.

Therefore, the correct legal and clinical remedy is a REMAND.

V. ORDER AND INSTRUCTIONS TO THE PLAN
HealthFirst is hereby ordered to take the following actions within five (5) business days of this determination:
1. Vacate the defective denial notice dated October 5, 2024.
2. Reissue a legally compliant denial notice to the member and the requesting provider that:
   a. Explicitly cites HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2.
   b. Details the specific clinical shortfalls (completion of only 4 of 6 weeks of physical therapy, trial of only 1 of 2 required pharmacological agents, and lack of interventional treatment).
   c. Addresses the member's claim of a functional plateau and explains why it does not meet the exception under CIC § 10169.5 (due to the lack of documentation of a plateau by the treating therapist or physician, and the outstanding pharmacotherapy and interventional requirements).
   d. Includes the mandatory California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) Independent Medical Review (IMR) application and notice of rights, as required by CHSC § 1374.31.

### **INDEPENDENT MEDICAL APPEAL DETERMINATION**

**Date of Determination:** November 14, 2024  
**Case ID:** PA-2024-E001  
**Member Name:** Victor Patel  
**Member ID:** M-667799  
**Age:** 60  
**Health Plan:** HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441  
**State of Residence:** California  
**Coverage Effective Date:** May 1, 2016  

**Requested Procedure:** Two-Level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6 and C6-C7  
**CPT Codes:** 22551 (Single-Level Cervical Decompression & Fusion) and 22552 (Each Additional Level)  
**Requesting Provider:** Dr. Lisa Park, MD — Spine Surgery, UCSF Medical Center  
**Date of Initial Denial:** November 1-2024  
**Initial Reviewer:** Dr. Patricia Huang, MD  
**Denial Reason Code:** MED-003  

---

### **FINAL DISPOSITION**
**OVERTURNED IN FULL:** The Health Plan’s decision to deny coverage for the second level of the requested surgery (C6-C7, CPT Code 22552) is **OVERTURNED**. The health plan is directed to authorize and cover the two-level ACDF at C5-C6 and C6-C7 as medically necessary under California law.

---

### **EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**
This case involves a first-level administrative and clinical appeal for a 60-year-old male member seeking authorization for a two-level ACDF (C5-C6 and C6-C7). The Health Plan initially approved the C5-C6 level but denied the adjacent C6-C7 level, asserting that the imaging for C6-C7 showed "mild changes only" and that plan criteria do not support a two-level fusion when only one level meets criteria. 

An exhaustive evaluation of the administrative record, clinical records, and governing legal frameworks was performed. This review applied the mandatory **Source Hierarchy for Conflict Resolution**: **California State Law & Regulations > Generally Accepted Clinical Standards > Health Plan Internal Criteria**.

The denial is overturned based on a critical, fatal **procedural notice defect** under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b). Under California law, this defect invalidates the health plan's denial, requiring an immediate **Overturn** of the decision. Additionally, a complete clinical analysis is provided below to establish a comprehensive baseline for this determination.

---

### **DETAILED ANALYSIS & EVALUATION**

#### **STEP 1: PROCEDURAL ADEQUACY AND DEFECT CHECK (CHSC § 1374.31(b))**
Under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b), any health plan medical necessity denial must meet strict statutory notice requirements. Specifically, a denial notice must explicitly specify the clinical criteria applied (e.g., *HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024*) and detail the specific clinical/imaging reasons supporting the denial. 

A review of the health plan's initial denial notice dated November 1, 2024, reveals the following:
1. **Failure to Cite Specific Criteria:** The denial notice failed to cite the health plan's specific internal clinical coverage guideline utilized for the review (e.g., *HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024*).
2. **Defective Clinical Explanation:** The denial text consisted of a brief, conclusory assertion (*"C6-C7 shows mild changes only. Two-level fusion not approved when one level meets criteria and one does not."*). It failed to provide the necessary objective radiological or clinical details mapping the imaging findings to the member’s presentation.

**Statutory Finding:** Under CHSC § 1374.31(b), a denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason for the denial is legally **defective** and "shall be treated as if no denial was issued." 

**Procedural Determination:** Because the plan's initial denial is procedurally defective under California law, the denial is legally invalid. Applying the Source Hierarchy of Authority, California statutory requirements supersede any internal health plan policies. Therefore, this procedural defect triggers an automatic **OVERTURN** of the plan's denial of CPT 22552.

---

#### **STEP 2: DIAGNOSTIC CLASSIFICATION AND SEVERITY EVALUATION**
To establish a complete clinical baseline, the patient’s primary clinical diagnosis was reviewed to determine if standard or modified conservative treatment pathways apply.

* **Cervical Myelopathy Criteria:** Diagnostic standards (AANS/CNS 2023; AO Spine 2021) require the presence of spinal cord compression on MRI, objective upper motor neuron (UMN) signs (e.g., positive Hoffman sign, hyperreflexia, clonus, gait instability), and bilateral symptoms.
* **Review of Clinical Record:** 
  * The neurological exam dated September 20, 2024, shows right bicep weakness (3+/5), an absent right bicep reflex, and right C6 dermatomal numbness and tingling.
  * No UMN signs were documented. Hoffman sign was absent, reflex findings were diminished/absent (consistent with lower motor neuron/nerve root compression), and no gait disturbances were noted.
  * MRI findings from September 15, 2024, confirmed moderate-severe right C6 nerve root compression at C5-C6 but showed no spinal cord contact or central cord compression at either level.

**Clinical Classification:** The member does not have Cervical Myelopathy. The clinical presentation is classified as **Cervical Radiculopathy** (specifically, severe right-sided C6 radiculopathy due to structural nerve root compression at C5-C6). Therefore, standard conservative treatment guidelines apply, and the Myelopathy Exception under CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2(A) is not triggered.

---

#### **STEP 3: IMAGING AND MULTI-LEVEL PATHOLOGY CORRELATION**
A clinical evaluation of the requested surgical levels was performed to correlate the MRI findings with the physical examinations:

1. **C5-C6 Level (Medically Necessary):**
   * **MRI (2024-09-15):** Large disc herniation, moderate-to-severe right C6 nerve root compression, and foraminal stenosis.
   * **Neurological Exam (2024-09-20):** 3+/5 right bicep weakness, absent right bicep reflex, and right C6 dermatomal paresthesias.
   * **Conservative Trial:** The patient completed 8 weeks (24 sessions) of physical therapy where C6 symptoms persisted. The patient trialed Pregabalin (4 months) and Naproxen (3 months) with partial relief. A right C6 epidural steroid injection on October 15, 2024, provided 70% relief, but symptoms fully returned after 4 weeks.
   * **Correlation:** The clinical and radiographic findings perfectly match. This level satisfies all criteria under *HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024* Section 2.1(a) and 2.2.

2. **C6-C7 Level (Clinically Indeterminate):**
   * **MRI (2024-09-15):** Small disc bulge, mild foraminal narrowing, no identifiable nerve root compression, and no cord contact.
   * **Neurological Exam (2024-09-20):** Right tricep reflex slightly diminished. No definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms. The physician noted mild C7 symptoms were "possibly present but not clearly documented."
   * **Conservative Trial:** Physical therapy notes at week 8 explicitly state that any potential C7 symptoms were "minimal and possibly resolving."
   * **Correlation:** The imaging findings of mild, age-related changes at C6-C7 do not correlate with a definitive, objective neurological deficit. While the surgeon argued that adjacent-level decompression and fusion should be addressed simultaneously to prevent accelerated degeneration, generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS 2023; NASS 2020) do not support prophylactic multi-level fusions in the absence of matching structural and clinical pathology.

**Clinical Finding:** From a purely clinical standpoint, the C6-C7 level does not independently meet standard medical necessity criteria. However, because the health plan issued a legally defective denial notice, this clinical deficit is superseded by the statutory remedy under California law.

---

#### **STEP 4: STATUTORY AND CLINICAL STANDARD OVERRIDE ANALYSIS**
According to the Source Hierarchy of Authority:
$$\text{California State Law \& Regulations} > \text{Clinical Standards} > \text{Health Plan Internal Criteria}$$

1. **Plan Criteria Application:** Under internal plan criteria (*CC-SPINE-2024* Section 3.3), the health plan denied C6-C7 due to lack of correlating imaging findings.
2. **Clinical Standards Application:** Generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS 2023) agree that prophylactic adjacent-segment fusion is not indicated for mild, asymptomatic degenerative changes.
3. **California State Law Application (CHSC § 1374.31(b)):** California law mandates that a plan's denial notice must be procedurally adequate, specifying the criteria and clinical reasoning applied. A failure to do so renders the denial **void**.

Because California State Law holds the highest position in the hierarchy, its statutory requirements override both the health plan's internal medical necessity criteria and the clinical standards. The health plan's procedural failure to issue a valid denial notice legally invalidates its decision to deny the C6-C7 level.

---

#### **STEP 5: DISPOSITION DETERMINATION**
Following the mandated Prior Authorization Appeal Decision Tree:
1. **Procedural adequacy check fails** due to the defective denial notice (omission of clinical criteria and lack of detailed clinical reasoning).
2. Pursuant to **CHSC § 1374.31(b)**, the denial is treated as if it was not issued.
3. The appeal must proceed directly to an **OVERTURN** disposition.

---

### **FORMAL ORDER OF THE REVIEWER**
The health plan is hereby ordered to **OVERTURN** its initial denial under Case ID **PA-2024-E001**. 

* **Approved Services:** Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF), two levels, C5-C6 and C6-C7.
* **Approved CPT Codes:** 22551 and 22552.
* **Facility:** UCSF Medical Center.
* **Provider:** Dr. Lisa Park, MD — Spine Surgery.

The health plan must issue a formal authorization letter to the member and the requesting provider within **five (5) business days** of receipt of this determination, in accordance with California Health & Safety Code § 1367.01.

A bilateral epidural injection targeting both levels should be tried before C6-C7 is reconsidered.

APPEAL DETERMINATION LETTER

Date: November 26, 2024

Member Name: Michael Green

Original Denial Date: November 8, 2024
Appeal Date: November 22, 2024
Reviewer: Independent Appeals Committee

FINAL DISPOSITION: OVERTURNED

Dear Mr. Green and Dr. Kim,

The HealthFirst Appeals and Grievances Department has completed its review of the first-level appeal submitted on November 22, 2024, regarding the prior authorization denial for a one-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6 (CPT 22551). 

After a comprehensive review of the clinical record, the HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria, California regulatory requirements, and generally accepted clinical standards, we have determined that the original denial issued on November 8, 2024, by Dr. Patricia Huang, MD, must be OVERTURNED. The requested surgical procedure is approved.

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The prior authorization request was originally denied under reason code MED-003, stating that the member did not meet plan criteria. However, our appeal review demonstrates that:
1. Clinically, the member fully satisfies all medical necessity criteria outlined in HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, including diagnostic, imaging, and conservative treatment requirements.
2. Procedurally, the original denial notice was legally defective under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31 because it failed to provide the referenced clinical criteria document and omitted the mandatory Independent Medical Review (IMR) notice.
3. Under California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5, the plan is prohibited from requiring further physical therapy as the member has already completed a 7-week course and reached a documented functional plateau.

II. CLINICAL COMPLIANCE WITH PLAN COVERAGE CRITERIA (CC-SPINE-2024)
A detailed review of the clinical record against HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024 (Effective January 1, 2024) confirms full compliance with all authorization requirements:

1. Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1(a)):
The member has a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy with objective neurological deficits. 
- Clinical Evidence: Dr. Kim's neurological examination on September 25, 2024, documented left C6 dermatomal numbness, a diminished left bicep reflex, and left bicep weakness graded at 4/5. This represents a clear, objective dermatomal neurological deficit correlating with the C5-C6 level.

2. Imaging Requirement (Section 2.1 & 2.3):
- Clinical Evidence: An MRI of the cervical spine dated September 20, 2024 (within the required 6-month window), demonstrated a large disc herniation at C5-C6 causing moderate left C6 nerve root compression. This structural pathology directly correlates with the member's left-sided C6 radicular symptoms and objective neurological deficits.

3. Conservative Treatment Requirement (Section 2.2):
The member has completed a comprehensive, documented course of conservative therapy that meets and exceeds all plan requirements:
- Physical Therapy (Section 2.2(a)): The criteria require a minimum of 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy. The clinical record documents that the member completed 7 weeks (total of 21 sessions) of supervised physical therapy. The physical therapy notes explicitly document that the member reached a functional plateau at week 6, with persistent radicular symptoms.
- Pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)): The criteria require a trial of at least two specified classes of medications for a minimum of 4 weeks each. The member trialed:
  - Gabapentin (Neuropathic agent) at 600mg TID for 4 months (16 weeks), which provided only partial relief.
  - Naproxen (NSAID) at 500mg BID for 3 months (12 weeks), which provided inadequate relief.
  Both trials far exceed the 4-week minimum duration.
- Interventional Treatment (Section 2.2(c)): The criteria require at least one interventional treatment. The member underwent a left C6 cervical epidural steroid injection on October 28, 2024, which provided 40% temporary relief before symptoms returned to baseline within 3 weeks.

4. Physician Documentation (Section 2.4):
The clinical record submitted by Dr. Sarah Kim, MD, contains the necessary clinical rationale, description of functional limitations, and documentation of failed conservative treatments, satisfying Section 2.4.

III. REGULATORY COMPLIANCE AND PROCEDURAL DEFECTS
Under California law, the original denial notice issued on November 8, 2024, contained critical procedural defects that independently invalidate the denial:

1. Failure to Provide Criteria and IMR Notice (CHSC § 1374.31):
- CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2) mandates that any medical necessity denial notice must include the specific clinical criteria applied and a notice of the member's Independent Medical Review (IMR) rights.
- The original denial notice referenced an attached criteria document, but no document was attached, and no IMR notice was included. Both the member and provider confirmed that no attachments were received.
- Under CHSC § 1374.31(b), a denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied is legally DEFECTIVE and must be treated as if no denial was issued for the purposes of appeal timelines.

2. Mechanical Application of Physical Therapy Requirements (CIC § 10169.5):
- CIC § 10169.5(a)(2) states that a health insurer shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy if the member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms.
- CIC § 10169.5(c) prohibits plans from mechanically applying a minimum number of weeks of physical therapy without reference to whether a functional plateau was achieved.
- Because the member completed 7 weeks of PT and reached a documented functional plateau at week 6, any denial based on a perceived failure to complete further physical therapy is a direct violation of California Insurance Code.

IV. ALIGNMENT WITH GENERALLY ACCEPTED CLINICAL STANDARDS
The requested ACDF at C5-C6 is highly aligned with generally accepted standards of medical practice:
- NASS Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020) and AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) classify cervical radiculopathy with persistent symptoms and objective neurological deficits (such as bicep weakness and diminished reflexes) that have failed to respond to 6–12 weeks of conservative care as a Tier 2 (Reasonable Indication) for surgical decompression.
- Delaying surgical intervention in a patient with objective, progressive motor weakness (4/5 bicep weakness) and a documented functional plateau in conservative therapy is clinically inappropriate and increases the risk of permanent neurological deficit.
- According to California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) Independent Medical Review (IMR) data from 2023, cervical spine denials are overturned at a rate of 72.3%, with the most common reason being that conservative treatment had already been completed (38% of overturns).

V. CONCLUSION AND AUTHORIZATION DETAILS
Because the member meets all clinical criteria under CC-SPINE-2024, and because the original denial notice was procedurally defective under California law (CHSC § 1374.31 and CIC § 10169.5), the prior authorization denial is hereby OVERTURNED.

Authorization Details:
- Approved Procedure: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C5-C6, one level (CPT 22551)
- Requesting Provider: Dr. Sarah Kim, MD (Cedars-Sinai Medical Center)
- Authorization Period: Valid for 90 days from the date of this letter (expires February 24, 2025) per CC-SPINE-2024 Section 3.5.

If you have any questions regarding this determination, please contact the Appeals and Grievances Department at 1-800-555-0199.

HealthFirst Health Plan

**HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN — APPEAL DETERMINATION**

**Case ID:** PA-2024-E002
**Member Name:** Catherine Mills
**Member ID:** M-778811
**Procedure Requested:** CPT 22551 – Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C3-C4, C4-C5, and C5-C6 (three levels)
**Requesting Provider:** Dr. James Torres, MD (Neurosurgery)
**Initial Denial Date:** 2024-11-25
**Reviewer:** Dr. [Your Name/Reviewer Title], MD

**DISPOSITION: OVERTURN**

**WARRANT:**

The denial for CPT 22551 for a three-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C3-C4, C4-C5, and C5-C6 is **OVERTURNED**. The requested procedure is medically necessary and meets generally accepted standards of medical practice, overriding the plan's more restrictive criteria where conflicts arise, as mandated by California state law.

**Detailed Rationale:**

1.  **Primary Diagnosis of Urgent Cervical Myelopathy:**
    *   The member, Catherine Mills, presents with a confirmed diagnosis of moderate to severe cervical myelopathy, which is the primary and most urgent clinical concern.
    *   **Clinical Evidence:** MRI (2024-10-01) reveals severe cord compression and T2 signal change (myelomalacia) at C4-C5. Neurological exam (2024-10-05) documents objective upper motor neuron signs including bilateral hyperreflexia, bilateral Hoffman sign, wide-based gait, and bilateral deltoid weakness. The presenting diagnosis includes "Multi-level cervical spondylosis with myeloradiculopathy," and conservative treatment notes confirm myelopathic symptoms stable but not improved.
    *   **Applicable Standards:** This clinical presentation unequivocally meets HealthFirst's Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.1(b) (Diagnosis Requirement for Cervical Myelopathy). Furthermore, AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) and NASS Guidelines (2020) classify this as a TIER 1 strong surgical indication (Section 3.1 of Clinical Evidence Base). Myelomalacia is a critical finding, indicating existing cord injury and surgical urgency (Section 1.2, Clinical Evidence Base).

2.  **Conservative Treatment Requirements Overridden by State Law and Clinical Standards:**
    *   The initial denial implicitly relies on HealthFirst's conservative treatment requirements, despite approving C4-C5. The denial of C3-C4 and C5-C6 based on "insufficient severity" may also be related to an expectation of further conservative treatment efficacy which is not applicable here.
    *   **California State Law Mandates Exception:**
        *   **DMHC All-Plan Letter APL 22-014 (Section II.1 & II.2):** Explicitly states that cervical myelopathy with objective evidence of cord compression and myelomalacia SHALL be treated as urgent, and plans SHALL NOT require completion of a full course of conservative treatment where objective imaging shows progressive pathology (myelomalacia) and conservative treatment has failed to arrest progression. This directly applies to Ms. Mills' case.
        *   **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(3):** Prohibits conditioning surgical approval on physical therapy (PT) completion where there is "objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address." Myelomalacia with severe cord compression falls squarely under this provision.
        *   **CIC § 10169.5(a)(2):** Also waives the PT requirement if the member has reached a functional plateau without adequate symptom resolution. Ms. Mills completed 9 weeks of PT, with myelopathic symptoms noted as "stable but not improved," indicating a functional plateau. Neurological symptoms in myelopathy are not expected to respond to PT regardless of duration (Section 5, Clinical Evidence Base).
    *   **Clinical Standards:** AO Spine Guidelines (2021) and AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) explicitly state there is no high-quality evidence supporting mandatory PT prior to surgery for moderate to severe cervical myelopathy. Delaying surgery in such patients for PT is not supported and may result in neurological deterioration (Section 2.1 & 2.3, Clinical Evidence Base). Myelomalacia is a contraindication to extended conservative treatment trials (Section 1.2, Clinical Evidence Base).
    *   **Conclusion:** The member has exceeded the conservative treatment duration that would be clinically appropriate or legally required for her condition. HealthFirst's standard conservative treatment requirements, or even its myelopathy exception, are superseded by state law and generally accepted clinical standards in this case.

3.  **Medical Necessity of All Three Levels (C3-C4, C4-C5, C5-C6):**
    *   **C4-C5 (Approved by initial reviewer):** Meets TIER 1 strong surgical indication due to severe cord compression, myelomalacia, and objective myelopathic signs (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020).
    *   **C5-C6 (Denied by initial reviewer):** Presents with moderate disc herniation, moderate left C6 nerve root compression, and objective neurological deficits including left bicep weakness (4-/5) and diminished bicep reflex. These persistent radicular symptoms with objective deficits, despite 9 weeks of PT and an epidural, meet HealthFirst's 2.1(a) and 2.1(c) diagnostic criteria and generally accepted clinical standards for surgical intervention (TIER 2 indication per AANS/CNS 2023). The initial denial's claim of "insufficient severity" is contradicted by the documented neurological findings and failed conservative treatment.
    *   **C3-C4 (Denied by initial reviewer):** Shows mild disc bulge and minimal foraminal narrowing. While less severe than the other levels, in the context of multi-level cervical spondylosis with significant myelopathy, surgical practice often includes contiguous levels with mild pathology that may contribute to symptoms or spinal instability, or to prevent adjacent segment disease. The treating surgeon's documented rationale for a three-level fusion, as stated in the appeal basis, supports this comprehensive approach. CHSC § 1374.32(b) mandates that if a service meets "generally accepted standards of medical practice," it SHALL be approved, even if the plan's internal criteria are more restrictive. Performing ACDF at three levels is not considered experimental (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024, Section 3.4).

**Conclusion:**

The member's severe cervical myelopathy with myelomalacia at C4-C5, combined with symptomatic radiculopathy at C5-C6 and multi-level spondylosis, necessitates surgical intervention. The conservative treatment requirements are overridden by California law and clinical standards due to the urgency and nature of myelopathy with myelomalacia. The denial of C3-C4 and C5-C6 on the basis of "insufficient severity" is not supported by the comprehensive clinical picture, objective findings, and accepted surgical principles for multi-level degenerative cervical disease. Therefore, the denial is **OVERTURNED**, and authorization for CPT 22551 (three-level ACDF C3-C4, C4-C5, C5-C6) is **APPROVED**.

**Sources Cited:**
*   HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria, CC-SPINE-2024.
*   California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5 (Effective 2023).
*   California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32(b).
*   DMHC All-Plan Letter APL 22-014 (Issued September 2022).
*   AANS/CNS Joint Section on Disorders of the Spine: Guidelines for Management of Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (2023 Update).
*   North American Spine Society (NASS): Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020).
*   AO Spine International: Clinical Practice Guideline (2021).

**Reviewer Signature:**
[Expert Health Plan Appeals Reviewer Name/Title]
HealthFirst Health Plan
ground_truth_answer: PARTIAL — (1) C4-C5: OVERTURN based on myelomalacia and CIC 10169.5(a)(3) regulatory override. (2) C5-C6: OVERTURN based on moderate compression, documented C6 neurological deficit, and met conservative treatment criteria. (3) C3-C4: UPHOLD — mild imaging findings, no specific radicular pattern documented, insufficient basis for surgical authorization at this level.
genuine_tension: Three levels requiring three separate analyses: C4-C5 (myelomalacia → regulatory override → clear OVERTURN), C5-C6 (moderate compression + C6 deficit + criteria met → likely OVERTURN), C3-C4 (mild changes + unclear symptoms → likely UPHOLD). The plan's binary denial gets the aggregate wrong even if it got one level right.

## II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF FINDINGS
An independent, hierarchy-based clinical appeal review has been conducted regarding the medical necessity of a three-level anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at C3-C4, C4-C5, and C5-C6. 

Based on California statutory mandates (CIC § 10169.5, CHSC § 1374.32(b), and DMHC APL 22-014), generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS 2023, AO Spine 2021), and HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024), a **Partial Approval** is mandated:

3.  **C3-C4** is denied because the imaging shows only mild degenerative changes without spinal cord or nerve root compression, and clinical evaluations confirm no localizing neurological deficits or clear symptomatic contribution, representing axial neck pain only.

---

## III. GOVERNING HIERARCHY OF AUTHORITY
Pursuant to California regulatory standards, where conflicts exist among reference sources, the following hierarchy of authority governs this review:
1.  **California State Law & Regulations:** California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5, California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.30-32, and Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014.
2.  **Generally Accepted Clinical Standards:** AANS/CNS Joint Section Guidelines (2023), AO Spine Clinical Practice Guidelines (2021), and North American Spine Society (NASS) Guidelines (2020).
3.  **Plan Clinical Criteria:** HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024).

---

## IV. STEP-BY-STEP EVALUATION & ANALYSIS

### STEP 1: Procedural Adequacy Review (CHSC § 1374.31(b))
The initial denial notice issued by Dr. Alan Foster on November 25, 2024, was analyzed. 
*   **Finding:** The denial notice stated: *"Three-level ACDF not approved. Review of imaging and clinical record supports surgical intervention at one level (C4-C5) only. C3-C4 and C5-C6 do not demonstrate pathology of sufficient severity to warrant surgical intervention at this time."*
*   **Procedural Deficiency:** This notice failed to cite the specific plan clinical policy document (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024) and failed to provide a detailed, individualized clinical explanation or specific clinical criteria applied to distinguish the pathology of C4-C5 from C5-C6.
*   **Regulatory Impact:** Under **CHSC § 1374.31(b)**, a denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason is **procedurally defective**. While this deficiency legally compromises the validity of the initial denial, this appeal proceeds to substantive clinical evaluation to issue a definitive, clinically sound decision.

---

### STEP 2: Clinical Classification & Diagnostic Verification
The clinical examination notes from Dr. James Torres (October 5, 2024) and the cervical spine MRI report (October 1, 2024) were reviewed to classify the disease process at each requested level:

*   **C3-C4 Level:** 
    *   *MRI Findings:* Mild disc bulge, minimal foraminal narrowing. No cord compression.
    *   *Clinical Exam:* Neck pain with palpation at C3-C4, but no specific radicular pattern.
    *   *PT Summary:* C3-C4 clinical contribution documented as "unclear."
    *   *Classification:* **Axial neck pain / Non-specific degenerative changes.**
*   **C4-C5 Level:** 
    *   *MRI Findings:* Large disc herniation, severe spinal cord compression, T2 signal change (myelomalacia).
    *   *Clinical Exam:* Myelopathy findings (bilateral hyperreflexia, bilateral Hoffman sign, wide-based gait); bilateral deltoid weakness (4/5, C5 distribution).
    *   *Classification:* **Moderate-to-Severe Cervical Myelopathy with Structural Cord Compromise.**
*   **C5-C6 Level:** 
    *   *MRI Findings:* Moderate disc herniation, moderate left C6 nerve root compression, foraminal stenosis.
    *   *Clinical Exam:* Left bicep weakness (4-/5), left bicep reflex diminished (C6 distribution).
    *   *PT Summary:* "C5-C6 radicular symptoms persist."
    *   *Classification:* **Cervical Radiculopathy (Left C6) with Objective Motor Deficit.**

---

### STEP 3: Plan Criteria & Internal Exception Compliance (CC-SPINE-2024)
The clinical facts were evaluated against HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria **CC-SPINE-2024**:

*   **C4-C5 Level (Myelopathy Exception 2.2(A)):**
    *   The member has confirmed cervical myelopathy (Section 2.1(b)) backed by objective MRI findings of severe cord compression and myelomalacia, and clinical findings of hyperreflexia, bilateral Hoffman, and gait disturbance.
    *   The member completed 9 weeks of physical therapy (exceeding the modified 4-week requirement under Section 2.2(A)).
    *   The member completed a trial of two neuropathic/muscle relaxant agents (Baclofen for 3 months, Pregabalin for 4 months), satisfying Section 2.2(b).
    *   *Compliance:* **Fully Met.**

*   **C5-C6 Level (Cervical Radiculopathy):**
    *   *Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1(a)):* Confirmed left C6 nerve root compression on MRI with corresponding dermatomal/motor deficits (diminished bicep reflex, bicep weakness). **Met.**
    *   *Conservative Treatment (Section 2.2):*
        *   *Physical Therapy:* Member completed **9 weeks (27 sessions)** of supervised physical therapy, exceeding the 6-week minimum. **Met.**
        *   *Pharmacotherapy:* Trial of at least two agents for 4+ weeks. Member trialed Baclofen (10mg TID for 3 months) and Pregabalin (300mg BID for 4 months). **Met.**
        *   *Interventional:* Epidural steroid injection performed on October 20, 2024 (documented "modest improvement in radicular symptoms"). **Met.**
    *   *Compliance:* **Fully Met.** The initial reviewer erred in denying C5-C6, as the clinical record shows complete compliance with all plan criteria for radiculopathy at this level.

*   **C3-C4 Level (Axial Pain Only):**
    *   *Exclusions (Section 3.1 & 3.3):* Section 3.1 explicitly excludes surgery performed solely for axial neck pain without radiculopathy or myelopathy. Section 3.3 excludes surgery when imaging does not demonstrate pathology consistent with clinical presentation.
    *   *Compliance:* **Not Met.** There is no objective radiculopathy or myelopathy correlating to C3-C4. Surgical intervention at C3-C4 is excluded under Sections 3.1 and 3.3 of the plan's policy.

---

### STEP 4: State Law & Regulatory Override Analysis (CIC § 10169.5 & DMHC APL 22-014)
California statutory provisions override plan clinical criteria where restrictive practices delay necessary neurological care:

*   **Application to C4-C5 (Myelopathy):**
    Under **CIC § 10169.5(a)(3)** and **DMHC APL 22-014**, plans cannot condition surgical approval on conservative therapy when objective imaging demonstrates structural neurological compromise (specifically myelomalacia/cord signal change) that physical therapy cannot address. Delaying surgery in the presence of active myelomalacia risks irreversible spinal cord injury. Statutory overrides mandate immediate approval of the C4-C5 level.
*   **Application to C5-C6 (Radiculopathy):**
    Under **CIC § 10169.5(a)(2)**, the plan is prohibited from requiring further conservative trials as the member completed a comprehensive PT course (9 weeks, 27 sessions) and the physical therapist/physician documented a functional plateau ("radicular symptoms persist").
*   **Application to C3-C4:**
    No statutory overrides apply to C3-C4. There is no cord compression, myelomalacia, or structural compromise at this level. The standard plan exclusions for axial neck pain are legally and clinically valid for C3-C4.

---

### STEP 5: Clinical Standard & Evidence-Based Guidelines Review (CHSC § 1374.32(b))
As mandated by **CHSC § 1374.32(b)**, the standard of review for medical necessity is based on generally accepted clinical standards, which override restrictive plan criteria:

*   **C4-C5 (Myelopathy):**
    *   *AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) / AO Spine Guidelines (2021):* Decompression is classified as a **Tier 1 (Strong) Indication** for moderate-to-severe myelopathy with spinal cord compression and myelomalacia. Standard clinical guidelines state there is no evidentiary basis for requiring physical therapy for moderate-to-severe myelopathy, and delay is strongly associated with permanent neurological deficits.
*   **C5-C6 (Radiculopathy):**
    *   *NASS Guidelines (2020) / AANS/CNS Guidelines (2023):* Decompression and fusion are indicated (**Tier 2**) for cervical radiculopathy with objective motor weakness (4-/5 left bicep weakness) that has failed to improve after 6–12 weeks of conservative management (9 weeks completed). Surgical decompression is medically necessary to prevent progressive motor deficits.
*   **C3-C4 (Axial Neck Pain):**
    *   *AANS/CNS Guidelines (2023) / NASS Guidelines (2020):* Surgery is classified as **Tier 3 (Not Indicated)** for axial neck pain in the absence of radicular symptoms, myelopathy, or correlating structural compression. Prophylactic multi-level fusion at an asymptomatic level showing only mild degenerative changes is not supported by clinical evidence and carries unnecessary surgical risk.

---

## V. LEVEL-BY-LEVEL DETERMINATION DETAILS

### 1. Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C4-C5 — APPROVED
*   **Clinical Basis:** The patient exhibits severe spinal cord compression with active myelomalacia (T2 signal change) on MRI, presenting clinically with gait disturbance, bilateral deltoid weakness (4/5), bilateral hyperreflexia, and a positive Hoffman sign.
*   **Authority Citation:** **AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) Tier 1**; **DMHC APL 22-014** (myelomalacia constitutes a time-sensitive neurological condition overriding standard conservative requirements); **CIC § 10169.5(a)(3)**.

### 2. Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C5-C6 — APPROVED
*   **Clinical Basis:** The patient has a moderate left-sided C5-C6 disc herniation causing moderate left C6 nerve root compression. This correlates directly with objective clinical findings of C6 radiculopathy, including left bicep weakness (4-/5) and a diminished left bicep reflex. The member has failed a robust 9-week course of PT, multiple medications, and a cervical epidural steroid injection, meeting all criteria.
*   **Authority Citation:** **HealthFirst Plan Policy CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2**; **CIC § 10169.5(a)(2)** (functional plateau reached); **NASS Evidence-Based Guidelines (2020)**.

### 3. Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C3-C4 — DENIED
*   **Clinical Basis:** MRI shows only a mild disc bulge and minimal foraminal narrowing. The physical exam shows neck pain on palpation without any radiating dermatomal symptoms, motor deficits, or myelopathic signs localizing to this level. The physical therapy notes state that any clinical contribution from the C3-C4 level is "unclear." Surgical fusion at this level would constitute treatment for non-specific axial neck pain, which is clinically inappropriate.
*   **Authority Citation:** **HealthFirst Plan Policy CC-SPINE-2024 Section 3.1 & 3.3**; **AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) Tier 3 (Not Indicated)**.

---

## VI. INSTRUCTIONS TO THE PLAN & PARTIES
1.  **Authorization Adjustment:** The health plan is directed to adjust the prior authorization under Case ID **PA-2024-E002** to reflect approval of a **two-level ACDF (C4-C5 and C5-C6)** under CPT codes **22551** (Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion, single level) and **22552** (Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion, each additional level).
2.  **Exclusion of C3-C4:** CPT code **22552** for a second additional level (representing C3-C4) remains denied.
3.  **Notice of IMR Rights:** Pursuant to **CHSC § 1374.30**, the member retains the right to seek an Independent Medical Review (IMR) through the California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) for the denied C3-C4 level. The standard IMR application and instructions are enclosed with this determination.

This determination has been prepared by an expert health plan appeals reviewer in accordance with California statutory requirements and generally accepted clinical standards.

Mr. George Harris, a 48-year-old member, requested prior authorization for a revision anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6. This procedure is a revision of a prior C5-C6 fusion performed in 2021. The member's appeal asserts that:
*   A CT scan confirms pseudarthrosis (failure of fusion) at C5-C6.
*   Symptoms have returned and worsened since the 2021 fusion.
*   Revision criteria are met per the treating surgeon.

**3. Clinical Record Review:**

*   **Presenting Diagnosis:** Pseudarthrosis C5-C6 following prior ACDF 2021 — failed fusion. Symptoms recurred at 18 months and have worsened.
*   **Neurological Exam (2024-09-20):** Documents return of right C6 symptoms: bicep weakness 4/5 right, diminished bicep reflex right, C6 dermatomal numbness. These symptoms are noted to be worse than the preoperative baseline prior to the initial 2021 fusion. This clinical presentation is consistent with cervical radiculopathy.
*   **Imaging:**
    *   **MRI (2024-09-01):** Limited by hardware artifact; possible non-union but not conclusive.

**4. Application of Three-Source Hierarchy:**

As per the established hierarchy, State Law supersedes Clinical Standards, which in turn supersede Plan Criteria.

**4.1. HealthFirst Plan Clinical Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024) Review:**

The requested procedure (CPT 22551) is within the scope of CC-SPINE-2024.

*   **2.1 DIAGNOSIS REQUIREMENT:** The member presents with cervical radiculopathy (right C6 weakness, diminished reflex, numbness) secondary to pseudarthrosis, which aligns with criterion 2.1(a). Imaging (CT) confirms the structural pathology.
*   **2.2 CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT REQUIREMENT:**
    *   **(a) Physical Therapy:** The member completed 8 weeks of PT (plan requires minimum 6 weeks). **Met.**
    *   **(b) Pharmacotherapy:** The member trialed Naproxen for 4 months and Gabapentin for 3 months (plan requires two agents for minimum 4 weeks each). **Met.** (Gabapentin met the 4-week duration threshold; Naproxen also met.)
    *   **(c) Interventional Treatment:** The member had a cervical epidural steroid injection. **Met.**
    *   The "MYELOPATHY EXCEPTION" (2.2(A)) is not directly applicable as the primary clinical presentation is radiculopathy, not myelopathy.

*   **Denial's Stated Reason vs. Plan's Own Criteria:** The denial stated, "Revision criteria require documentation of hardware failure, pseudarthrosis, or new pathology at previously treated level. Documentation submitted does not confirm hardware failure." However, the member's CT scan unequivocally confirms "pseudarthrosis" and "failed fusion" at C5-C6, which is one of the *explicit criteria listed in the denial reason itself* for revision surgery. The denial's conclusion that documentation "does not confirm hardware failure" while ignoring the confirmed pseudarthrosis constitutes a direct misapplication and misinterpretation of its own stated criteria against the available clinical evidence.

**4.2. California Regulatory Framework Review:**

*   **CHSC § 1374.31(b) (Defective Denial Notice):** While the denial notice specifies criteria, its interpretation and application of those criteria against the submitted clinical documentation is factually incorrect and misleading.
*   **CIC § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy as Prerequisite):** This state law stipulates that a plan cannot condition approval on completion of PT where:
    *   (a)(1) The physician documents PT is unlikely to benefit given the nature of the condition: The treating physician explicitly noted PT "cannot address structural hardware/fusion failure." **Applicable.**
    *   (a)(2) The member completed PT and reached a functional plateau: The member completed 8 weeks of PT with "No improvement." This constitutes a functional plateau by clinical and regulatory definitions. **Applicable.**
    *   (a)(3) The condition involves objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that PT cannot address: Pseudarthrosis is a structural failure leading to objective C6 radiculopathy (weakness, diminished reflex, numbness). **Applicable.**

*   **DMHC APL 22-014 (Conservative Treatment Exceptions for Time-Sensitive Conditions):** Although primarily focused on myelopathy, Section II.2(a) states plans shall not require a full course of conservative treatment when "Objective imaging evidence demonstrates progressive pathology (cord signal change, myelomalacia, or progressive herniation on serial imaging)," and Section II.2(b) "Treating physician provides documentation that conservative treatment has been attempted and has failed to arrest progression." While not myelomalacia, pseudarthrosis is progressive structural pathology that has failed conservative treatment. Section II.3 further states plans shall not apply internal criteria more restrictive than generally accepted standards.
*   **CHSC § 1374.32(b) (IMR Standard):** This provision is paramount: Services meeting generally accepted standards of medical practice SHALL be approved regardless of whether the plan's internal criteria are more restrictive.

**4.3. Clinical Standard Review (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020, AO Spine 2021):**

*   **Diagnostic Classification:** The member's symptoms (unilateral C6 weakness, diminished reflex, numbness) are consistent with cervical radiculopathy (Clinical Reference Summary, Section 1.1). The underlying cause is failed fusion (pseudarthrosis).
*   **Conservative Treatment for Radiculopathy:** While conservative treatment is typically effective for radiculopathy, the clinical record clearly demonstrates a failure of an adequate conservative trial (8 weeks PT with no improvement, 3-4 months of two pharmacotherapies with partial/minimal relief, and an epidural with minimal improvement). The treating physician's assessment that PT cannot address structural failure is supported by the clinical evidence (Clinical Reference Summary, Section 2.1, 2.3 - risk of delay).
*   **Surgical Indications for ACDF (CPT 22551):** Per AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023), surgical intervention for radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks of conservative treatment, or significant functional impairment not responding to conservative care, is a TIER 2 reasonable indication (Clinical Reference Summary, Section 3.1). The member's presentation of persistent and worsening C6 radiculopathy due to a confirmed pseudarthrosis, despite an adequate conservative trial, meets this standard. Revision surgery for symptomatic pseudarthrosis is a generally accepted clinical practice.

**5. Disposition and Warrant:**

**DISPOSITION: OVERTURN**

**WARRANT:**

The denial for CPT 22551 (Revision ACDF C5-C6) for Mr. George Harris is **OVERTURNED** based on the following reasons:

1.  **Misapplication of Plan Criteria:** The initial denial letter itself stated that "Revision criteria require documentation of hardware failure, pseudarthrosis, or new pathology at previously treated level." However, the denial concluded, "Documentation submitted does not confirm hardware failure," ignoring the explicit finding of "pseudarthrosis" on the CT scan (2024-09-15). This represents a direct factual error and a misapplication of HealthFirst's *own stated criteria* against the submitted clinical documentation. The CT scan definitively confirms pseudarthrosis, which meets one of the plan's acknowledged criteria for revision surgery.

2.  **Plan's Conservative Treatment Criteria Met:** The member completed 8 weeks of physical therapy, a trial of two pharmacotherapy agents for 3-4 months, and one interventional procedure (epidural). This fully satisfies HealthFirst's conservative treatment requirements as outlined in Section 2.2(a), (b), and (c) of CC-SPINE-2024.
    *   *Source:* HealthFirst Plan Clinical Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2); Clinical Record (conservative treatment summary).

3.  **California State Law Override (CIC § 10169.5):** Even if the plan's conservative treatment requirements had not been met, California Insurance Code § 10169.5 specifically prohibits conditioning approval of surgery on physical therapy completion when:
    *   The treating physician documented PT is unlikely to benefit structural failure. (a)(1)
    *   The member completed PT and reached a functional plateau ("No improvement" after 8 weeks). (a)(2)
    *   The condition involves objective evidence of structural neurological compromise (pseudarthrosis causing C6 radiculopathy) that PT cannot address. (a)(3)
    All three conditions are met in this case.
    *   *Source:* California Insurance Code § 10169.5; Clinical Record (physical therapy summary, neurological exam).

4.  **Consistency with Generally Accepted Clinical Standards:** The member's persistent and worsening cervical radiculopathy (C6 weakness, diminished reflex, numbness) stemming from a confirmed pseudarthrosis (failed fusion) despite an adequate and failed course of conservative treatment (8 weeks PT, pharmacotherapy, epidural) meets generally accepted standards for surgical intervention. Surgical revision for symptomatic pseudarthrosis causing neurological deficits following failed conservative management is a recognized and recommended treatment.
    *   *Source:* AANS/CNS Joint Section on Disorders of the Spine: Guidelines for Management of Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (2023 Update, TIER 2 indication); North American Spine Society (NASS): Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020, TIER 2 indication); Clinical Reference Summary (Section 3.1, 4).
    *   Under CHSC § 1374.32(b), services meeting generally accepted standards of medical practice shall be approved regardless of the plan's internal criteria if they are more restrictive.

Based on the comprehensive review of the clinical documentation, HealthFirst's own criteria, California state law, and generally accepted clinical standards, the requested revision ACDF at C5-C6 for Mr. George Harris is medically necessary.

### FORMAL DISPOSITION
The initial adverse determination issued by HealthFirst on October 30, 2024, denying authorization for CPT code 22551 (Revision ACDF C5-C6) at UCSF Medical Center is **OVERTURNED** in its entirety. 

HealthFirst is hereby ordered to **APPROVE** and authorize the requested surgical procedure immediately.

---

### EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF DETERMINATION
An independent clinical and regulatory evaluation of this appeal was conducted utilizing the mandated California Hierarchy of Authority. 

The denial was overturned based on three independent and compounding grounds:
1. **Procedural Defect (CHSC § 1374.31(b)):** The initial denial notice issued by Dr. Patricia Huang was legally defective. It failed to cite the specific clinical coverage policy applied (CC-SPINE-2024), failed to provide a valid clinical rationale by ignoring documented pseudarthrosis (which was listed as a criteria element), and failed to provide mandated California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) Independent Medical Review (IMR) disclosures.
2. **Satisfaction of Plan Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024):** The medical record demonstrates that the member fully satisfied the plan’s standard clinical criteria. The plan’s reviewer committed a severe clinical error by stating that the member did not qualify because the documentation "does not confirm hardware failure," completely ignoring that both the plan's guidelines and the denial text itself establish **pseudarthrosis** as an independent qualifying indication. The member's CT scan dated September 15, 2024, unequivocally confirms C5-C6 pseudarthrosis (failed fusion). Furthermore, the member fully completed and exhausted all standard conservative therapy requirements.
3. **Clinical Standard of Medical Necessity (CHSC § 1374.32(b)):** National clinical guidelines from the American Association of Neurological Surgeons/Congress of Neurological Surgeons (AANS/CNS 2023), the North American Spine Society (NASS 2020), and AO Spine (2021) establish that surgical revision is the standard of care for symptomatic, imaging-confirmed pseudarthrosis associated with an objective neurological deficit (4/5 bicep weakness) that has failed to improve with conservative trials. Under California law, these clinical standards override restrictive or misapplied plan criteria.

---

### DETAILED EVALUATION FINDINGS

#### 1. Procedural Defect Check (California Health & Safety Code § 1374.31(b))
Under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b), a health plan's denial notice is legally defective if it fails to specify the exact clinical coverage guidelines applied, fails to provide a clear, logically consistent clinical reason for the denial, or fails to include mandated notifications of California state Independent Medical Review (IMR) rights.

*   **Policy Citation Omission:** The initial denial notice dated October 30, 2024, vaguely referenced "standard ACDF criteria" and "Revision criteria" but failed to cite the specific governing policy document (**HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024**).
*   **Logical and Clinical Contradiction:** The denial letter stated: *"Revision criteria require documentation of hardware failure, pseudarthrosis, or new pathology at previously treated level. Documentation submitted does not confirm hardware failure."* By restricting approval *solely* to hardware failure, the plan reviewer ignored the member's documented pseudarthrosis, which the reviewer had just admitted was an alternative qualifying criterion. 
*   **Missing Disclosures:** The denial notice failed to include the mandatory statutory language detailing the member’s right to request an IMR through the DMHC.
*   **Procedural Finding:** **Positive (Defect Present).** The denial notice is procedurally and legally defective under CHSC § 1374.31(b), which is sufficient grounds to overturn the adverse determination.

#### 2. Clinical Classification & Diagnostic Verification
To ensure correct guideline application, the clinical record was analyzed to classify the underlying pathology:
*   **Neurological Examination Findings (2024-09-20):** Diminished right bicep reflex, 4/5 right bicep weakness, and C6 dermatomal numbness. These findings represent a lower motor neuron deficit consistent with unilateral C6 radiculopathy.
*   **Imaging Findings:** The cervical spine MRI (2024-09-01) and CT scan (2024-09-15) demonstrate no evidence of spinal cord compression, T2 cord signal changes (myelomalacia), or upper motor neuron (UMN) signs (e.g., Hoffman sign, hyperreflexia, clonus, gait instability, or bilateral weakness).
*   **Diagnostic Finding:** The member's condition is classified as **Cervical Radiculopathy secondary to C5-C6 Pseudarthrosis (failed fusion)**. While the "Myelopathy Pathway" (Exception 2.2(A)) does not apply, the case must be evaluated under the standard cervical radiculopathy and revision criteria.

#### 3. Review of Revision-Specific Plan Criteria vs. Clinical Facts
The clinical record was cross-referenced against HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria **CC-SPINE-2024** to determine compliance:

##### A. Revision Criteria Validation
The plan’s coverage criteria permit revision surgery at a previously treated level if there is objective documentation of **hardware failure, pseudarthrosis, or new pathology**.
*   **Imaging Evidence:** The thin-cut cervical CT scan dated September 15, 2024 (which is free from the hardware artifact that limited the September 1, 2024 MRI) explicitly states: *"C5-C6 — incomplete bridging bone formation. Lucency around hardware suggesting pseudarthrosis. Findings consistent with failed fusion/pseudarthrosis."*
*   **Clinical Determination:** The member has documented, symptomatic pseudarthrosis at the C5-C6 level. The plan's assertion that the surgery must be denied because there is no "hardware failure" is a direct misapplication of its own clinical criteria, which lists pseudarthrosis as an independent, stand-alone indication for revision.

##### B. Conservative Treatment Compliance (CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2)
The plan requires a documented course of conservative treatment before surgical authorization. The clinical record demonstrates that the member has not only met but exceeded these requirements:
1.  **Physical Therapy (Section 2.2(a)):** Requires a minimum of 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy. 
    *   *Member's Compliance:* The member completed **8 weeks (24 sessions) of supervised physical therapy**. The physical therapist and treating physician documented that the member achieved no clinical improvement and reached a functional plateau, noting that physical therapy cannot structurally address a non-union/failed spinal fusion.
2.  **Pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)):** Requires a trial of at least two qualifying agents for a minimum of 4 weeks each.
    *   *Member's Compliance:* The member completed a **4-month trial of Naproxen 500mg BID** (NSAID) and a **3-month trial of Gabapentin 300mg TID** (neuropathic agent). Both trials yielded only partial, temporary relief.
3.  **Interventional Treatment (Section 2.2(c)):** Requires at least one interventional treatment (e.g., epidural steroid injection).
    *   *Member's Compliance:* The member underwent a **cervical epidural steroid injection on October 10, 2024**, which resulted in minimal clinical improvement.
*   **Substantive Finding:** The member fully satisfied all standard conservative treatment and imaging criteria under CC-SPINE-2024. The plan erred in denying the request on conservative treatment grounds.

#### 4. Application of California Statutory and Regulatory Overrides
Under **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(2)**, a health plan is legally prohibited from conditioning the approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of additional physical therapy if:
> *"The member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms."*

The clinical record confirms the member completed 24 sessions of physical therapy and reached a clear functional plateau due to the structural nature of the failed fusion (pseudarthrosis). Under CIC § 10169.5, the plan cannot legally require any additional conservative therapy trials.

#### 5. Evaluation of Clinical Standard of Care (CHSC § 1374.32(b))
Pursuant to **California Health & Safety Code § 1374.32(b)**, the standard of medical necessity for an appeal review must align with generally accepted standards of medical practice rather than a health plan's restrictive internal guidelines.

*   **AANS/CNS (2023 Joint Guidelines) & NASS (2020 Guidelines):** These national authorities establish that surgical revision is indicated and medically necessary for patients who present with:
    1.  Objective imaging evidence of pseudarthrosis (failed fusion) at a prior surgical level;
    2.  Recurrent or worsening radicular symptoms corresponding to that level;
    3.  An objective neurological deficit (e.g., 4/5 motor weakness); and
    4.  Failure to respond to a comprehensive course of conservative management (including physical therapy, pharmacotherapy, and interventional injections).
*   **Clinical Practice Standard:** Delaying surgical stabilization and decompression in a patient with an active motor deficit (4/5 bicep weakness) and confirmed pseudarthrosis poses an unnecessary risk of permanent nerve root injury. 
*   **Standard of Care Finding:** The requested CPT code 22551 for Revision ACDF C5-C6 represents the standard of care for this clinical presentation and is highly medically necessary.

---

### FORMAL ORDER & INSTRUCTIONS TO THE PLAN
Based on the foregoing evaluation, the initial denial is **OVERTURNED**. 

HealthFirst is hereby ordered to take the following actions:
1.  **Authorize CPT Code 22551** (Revision ACDF C5-C6) at UCSF Medical Center, as requested by Dr. Karen Williams, MD.
2.  **Issue the written authorization** to the member and the requesting provider within **two (2) business days** of receipt of this determination, in accordance with California regulatory timelines.
3.  **Waive any further conservative treatment prerequisites**, as the member has fully exhausted all clinically appropriate conservative measures and met all statutory requirements under CIC § 10169.5.

**Authorized by:**  
*Medical Appeal Reviewer, Board-Certified Orthopaedic / Neurological Spine Surgery Specialist*  
**Date of Determination:** November 4, 2024

FINAL APPEAL DETERMINATION: PARTIAL OVERTURN

Dear Ms. Mills and Dr. Torres,

HealthFirst Health Plan has completed its clinical and regulatory review of the appeal submitted on December 10, 2024, regarding the prior authorization denial for a three-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C3-C4, C4-C5, and C5-C6 (CPT 22551 x3). 

Based on a comprehensive review of the clinical record, California regulatory requirements, and generally accepted clinical standards, HealthFirst has issued a PARTIAL OVERTURN of the initial denial. The level-by-level determinations are as follows:

1. C4-C5 Level: OVERTURNED (Approved for surgery)
2. C5-C6 Level: OVERTURNED (Approved for surgery)
3. C3-C4 Level: UPHELD (Denied for surgery)

A detailed clinical and regulatory rationale for each level is provided below.

---

I. CLINICAL PRESENTATION SUMMARY
The member is a 53-year-old female presenting with multi-level cervical spondylosis with myeloradiculopathy. 
- Cervical MRI (dated October 1, 2024) demonstrates:
  - C3-C4: Mild disc bulge, minimal foraminal narrowing.
  - C4-C5: Large disc herniation, severe spinal cord compression, and T2 signal change within the spinal cord (myelomalacia).
  - C5-C6: Moderate disc herniation, moderate left C6 nerve root compression, and foraminal stenosis.
- Neurological Examination (dated October 5, 2024) reveals:
  - Myelopathic findings: Bilateral hyperreflexia, bilateral Hoffman sign, and a wide-based gait.
  - C5 level: Bilateral deltoid weakness (4/5).
  - C6 level: Left bicep weakness (4-/5) and diminished left bicep reflex.
  - C4 level: Unclear clinical correlation; neck pain is present with C3-C4 palpation, but there is no specific radicular pattern.
- Conservative Treatment History:
  - Physical Therapy (PT): Completed 9 weeks (27 sessions). The physical therapist documented that myelopathic symptoms remained stable but unimproved, C5-C6 radicular symptoms persisted, and the C3-C4 contribution remained unclear.
  - Pharmacotherapy: Completed a 3-month trial of Baclofen 10mg TID (minimal spasticity relief) and a 4-month trial of Pregabalin 300mg BID (partial pain relief).
  - Interventional: Cervical epidural steroid injection on October 20, 2024, resulting in modest improvement in radicular symptoms but no change in myelopathic signs.

---

II. LEVEL-BY-LEVEL CLINICAL AND REGULATORY ANALYSIS

1. LEVEL C4-C5: OVERTURNED (APPROVED)
- Plan Criteria Alignment: The clinical record satisfies HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.1(b) (Cervical Myelopathy), as the member exhibits objective spinal cord compression on MRI and multiple myelopathic symptoms (gait disturbance, hyperreflexia, bilateral Hoffman sign). Under Section 2.2 Exception (Myelopathy Pathway), the conservative treatment requirement is modified, reducing the physical therapy requirement to 4 weeks (the member completed 9 weeks) and waiving the interventional treatment requirement if documented as a risk (though the member completed an epidural regardless).
- Regulatory Requirements: Under California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014, Section II.1, cervical myelopathy with objective evidence of cord compression and myelomalacia on MRI constitutes a condition with potential for irreversible harm. Section II.2 mandates that plans shall not require a full course of conservative treatment when objective imaging demonstrates progressive pathology (such as myelomalacia) and the clinical standard indicates surgery. Furthermore, California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(3) prohibits conditioning surgical approval on physical therapy where there is objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address.
- Clinical Standards: Under the AANS/CNS Joint Section Guidelines for Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (2023) and AO Spine International Guidelines (2021), the presence of moderate-to-severe myelopathy with myelomalacia (T2 signal change) is a Tier 1 (Strong Indication) for surgical decompression. Delaying surgery in this setting is associated with permanent neurological deficits.
- Conclusion: The denial of the C4-C5 level is overturned. Surgical intervention is approved.

2. LEVEL C5-C6: OVERTURNED (APPROVED)
- Plan Criteria Alignment: The clinical record satisfies CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.1(a) (Cervical Radiculopathy) and Section 2.1(c) (Cervical disc herniation with objective neurological deficit). The member has a moderate disc herniation at C5-C6 with moderate left C6 nerve root compression, corresponding to left bicep weakness (4-/5) and a diminished left bicep reflex. The member fully completed the conservative treatment requirements under Section 2.2: 9 weeks of PT (exceeding the 6-week requirement in 2.2(a)), two neuropathic/muscle relaxant medications for over 4 weeks each (exceeding 2.2(b)), and a cervical epidural steroid injection on October 20, 2024 (satisfying 2.2(c)).
- Regulatory Requirements: Under CIC § 10169.5(a)(2), a health plan cannot condition surgical approval on physical therapy where the member has completed a course of physical therapy and reached a functional plateau. The physical therapy summary explicitly notes that after 9 weeks, C5-C6 radicular symptoms persisted and a functional plateau was reached.
- Clinical Standards: Under the AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) and NASS Guidelines (2020), surgical decompression is a Tier 2 (Reasonable Indication) for radiculopathy with persistent symptoms and objective neurological deficits (weakness and reflex changes) that have failed to respond to 6-12 weeks of conservative care.
- Conclusion: The initial denial stated that C5-C6 did not demonstrate pathology of sufficient severity. This finding is contradicted by the objective MRI and neurological exam. Because the member met all plan criteria and clinical standards, the denial of the C5-C6 level is overturned. Surgical intervention is approved.

3. LEVEL C3-C4: UPHELD (DENIED)
- Plan Criteria Alignment: Under CC-SPINE-2024, Section 3.1, surgical authorization is excluded when requested solely for axial neck pain without documented radiculopathy or myelopathy. Section 3.3 further excludes coverage when imaging does not demonstrate pathology consistent with the clinical presentation. The MRI shows only a mild disc bulge and minimal foraminal narrowing at C3-C4. The neurological exam notes that the clinical contribution of this level is "unclear," with neck pain on palpation but no specific radicular pattern. The physical therapy records also state that the C3-C4 contribution is unclear.
- Regulatory Requirements: There are no regulatory overrides or provisions under California law (including CIC § 10169.5 or DMHC APL 22-014) that mandate coverage for a surgical level lacking objective pathology or correlating clinical deficits.
- Clinical Standards: Under the AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) Tier 3, surgical intervention is not indicated for axial neck pain in the absence of correlating radiculopathy or myelopathy, or where imaging findings do not correlate with symptoms.
- Conclusion: Because there is insufficient clinical or radiographic evidence to support surgical intervention at C3-C4, the denial of this level is upheld.

---

III. PROCEDURAL DEFECT IN INITIAL DENIAL NOTICE
Pursuant to California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b), a denial notice must specify the clinical criteria applied and the specific clinical reasons for the denial. The initial denial notice dated November 25, 2024, issued by Dr. Alan Foster, MD, failed to provide a level-by-level clinical analysis or specify the criteria used to deny the C5-C6 level, which fully met the plan's medical necessity criteria. Under California law, a denial notice that fails to specify these elements is procedurally defective. HealthFirst has corrected this defect through this comprehensive appeal determination.

---

IV. INDEPENDENT MEDICAL REVIEW (IMR) RIGHTS (FOR UPHELD LEVEL C3-C4)
If you disagree with the decision to uphold the denial of the C3-C4 level, you have the right to request an Independent Medical Review (IMR) from the California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC). 

Under California Health & Safety Code § 1374.30, you may submit an application for an IMR if your request for a health care service has been denied, modified, or delayed by the plan on the basis of medical necessity. 
- There is no cost to you for an IMR.
- The DMHC will make a decision within 30 days of receiving your completed application and supporting documentation (or within 3 days for urgent cases involving an imminent threat to your health).
- If the IMR decision is in your favor, HealthFirst is legally bound to accept the decision and authorize the service.

To apply for an IMR, please complete the Independent Medical Review Application Form enclosed with this letter or apply online at the DMHC website (www.dmhc.ca.gov). You may also contact the DMHC Help Center toll-free at 1-888-466-2219.
