HealthFirst has completed its first-level internal appeal review of the prior authorization request for a two-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the C5-C6 and C6-C7 levels. 

FINAL APPEAL DISPOSITION:
PARTIAL OVERTURN
- C5-C6 Level (CPT 22551): OVERTURNED (Approved for Clinical Coverage)
- C6-C7 Level (CPT 22552): UPHELD (Denied without prejudice)

Because a portion of this request has been denied, you have the right to immediately appeal this decision to an Independent Medical Review (IMR) through the California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC), as detailed at the end of this letter.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART I: PROCEDURAL ANALYSIS & DEEMED APPROVAL JUSTIFICATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b), a health plan's denial notice must specify the clinical criteria applied and the specific clinical reasons for the denial. The initial denial notice issued on November 1, 2024, failed to cite the specific clinical coverage criteria applied (HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024). Under § 1374.31(b), a defective notice is treated as if no denial was issued, which would technically trigger a "deemed approval" of the entire two-level request under CHSC § 1367.01 due to the expiration of the statutory 5-business-day decision window.

However, HealthFirst has determined that a strict mechanical application of procedural deemed approval to the entire request is overridden by paramount clinical safety standards and the prevention of unnecessary surgical harm. Performing an invasive spinal fusion at an asymptomatic level with only mild imaging findings (C6-C7) poses a significant risk of unnecessary surgical morbidity, adjacent segment disease, and permanent neurological risk without clinical benefit. Therefore, clinical-merit review and patient safety override procedural technicalities in this instance, necessitating a partial clinical overturn rather than a full procedural deemed approval.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART II: CLINICAL RATIONALE FOR C5-C6 LEVEL (CPT 22551) — OVERTURNED (APPROVED)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The request for ACDF at the C5-C6 level is medically necessary and meets all authorization requirements under HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2:

1. Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1): The member has a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy with objective neurological deficits (Section 2.1(a) & (c)). Clinical examination on September 20, 2024, documented right bicep weakness (3+/5), an absent right bicep reflex, and right C6 dermatomal numbness and tingling.
2. Imaging Requirement (Section 2.3): MRI dated September 15, 2024, demonstrates a large disc herniation, moderate-to-severe right C6 nerve root compression, and foraminal stenosis at the C5-C6 level, directly correlating with the member's C6 radicular symptoms.
3. Conservative Treatment Requirement (Section 2.2): 
   - Physical Therapy (Section 2.2(a)): The member completed 8 weeks (24 sessions) of supervised physical therapy directed at the cervical spine, exceeding the 6-week plan requirement.
   - Pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)): The member completed a trial of two qualifying agents for at least 4 weeks: Pregabalin (150mg BID for 4 months) and Naproxen (500mg BID for 3 months).
   - Interventional Treatment (Section 2.2(c)): The member underwent a right C6 epidural steroid injection on October 15, 2024, which provided 70% temporary relief but symptoms fully returned after 4 weeks.

This clinical presentation also satisfies Tier 2 (Reasonable Indication) of the AANS/CNS Joint Section Guidelines (2023) for cervical radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after conservative management. Accordingly, the denial for the C5-C6 level (CPT 22551) is OVERTURNED and approved.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART III: CLINICAL RATIONALE FOR C6-C7 LEVEL (CPT 22552) — UPHELD (DENIED WITHOUT PREJUDICE)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The request for ACDF at the C6-C7 level does not meet the medical necessity criteria under CC-SPINE-2024 or generally accepted clinical standards, and is therefore UPHELD (denied) without prejudice:

1. Insufficient Imaging Findings (Section 2.3 & Section 3.3): The MRI dated September 15, 2024, shows only a small disc bulge and mild foraminal narrowing at C6-C7. There is no identifiable nerve root compression and no spinal cord contact. Under Section 3.3, surgery is excluded when imaging does not demonstrate pathology consistent with the clinical presentation.
2. Lack of Correlating Neurological Deficits (Section 2.1): The neurological exam on September 20, 2024, noted a slightly diminished right tricep reflex, but no definitive C7 dermatomal symptoms (weakness, numbness, or tingling). The treating physician's notes state that mild C7 symptoms were "possibly present but not clearly documented."
3. Resolving Symptoms and Lack of Level-Specific Conservative Trials (Section 2.2): Physical therapy records at week 8 explicitly document that the member's C7-related symptoms were "minimal and possibly resolving." Furthermore, no level-specific interventional treatment (such as a C7-specific selective nerve root block or epidural injection) was performed to confirm that the C6-C7 level is a primary pain generator.

Under California's IMR standard of medical necessity (CHSC § 1374.32) and the AANS/CNS Joint Section Guidelines (2023), surgical decompression and fusion are not clinically appropriate or indicated (Tier 3) at a level lacking objective structural compression and correlating clinical symptoms. Performing a fusion at C6-C7 under these circumstances exposes the patient to unnecessary surgical risk.

GUIDANCE FOR RESUBMISSION (WITHOUT PREJUDICE):
Should the member's clinical condition change, HealthFirst will reconsider the C6-C7 level upon submission of the following objective clinical documentation:
1. An updated, detailed neurological examination clearly documenting persistent, reproducible C7 dermatomal symptoms (e.g., triceps weakness, C7 dermatomal sensory loss).
2. Diagnostic interventional evidence, such as a selective C7 nerve root block or a bilateral epidural injection targeting both levels, demonstrating level-specific pain reproduction or relief.
3. Updated cervical imaging if clinical symptoms significantly deteriorate.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART IV: IMPORTANT NOTICE OF RIGHT TO INDEPENDENT MEDICAL REVIEW (IMR)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If you disagree with our decision to uphold the denial of the C6-C7 level (CPT 22552), you have the right to request an Independent Medical Review (IMR) from the California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC). 

An IMR is an online or written review conducted by independent, board-certified specialists who are completely independent of HealthFirst. If the IMR reviewer decides that the requested service is medically necessary under CHSC § 1374.32, HealthFirst must authorize and cover the service. The IMR process is free to you.

You can apply for an IMR if your health plan has denied, modified, or delayed a health care service based on a decision that the service is not medically necessary. You must generally apply for an IMR within six (6) months of receiving this appeal determination letter.

To apply for an IMR, please contact the DMHC Help Center at 1-888-466-2219 or visit their website at www.dmhc.ca.gov to submit an application online.

Clinical Review Division

PROCEDURE REQUESTED: Revision Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C5-C6 (CPT 22551)
PRIOR AUTHORIZATION DENIAL DATE: October 30, 2024
DENIAL REVIEWER: Dr. Patricia Huang, MD
DISPOSITION: OVERTURNED ON APPEAL

Dear Mr. Harris and Dr. Williams,

The HealthFirst Appeals and Grievances Department has completed its review of the first-level clinical appeal submitted on behalf of George Harris regarding the prior authorization denial for a Revision Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the C5-C6 level (CPT code 22551).

After a comprehensive review of the clinical record, the plan's clinical coverage criteria, California regulatory requirements, and generally accepted clinical standards, HealthFirst has determined that the prior authorization denial issued on October 30, 2024, must be OVERTURNED. Authorization for the requested revision surgery at UCSF Medical Center is hereby APPROVED.

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The initial denial of prior authorization on October 30, 2024, by Dr. Patricia Huang, MD, was based on the rationale that "Revision surgery [is] not covered under standard ACDF criteria... Revision criteria require documentation of hardware failure, pseudarthrosis, or new pathology... Documentation submitted does not confirm hardware failure."

This appeal review has identified that the initial denial was clinically and procedurally flawed. The plan's reviewer failed to evaluate the appropriate imaging modality—the cervical CT scan dated September 15, 2024—which explicitly confirms pseudarthrosis (failed fusion) at C5-C6. Instead, the reviewer relied on an MRI dated September 1, 2024, which was explicitly noted by the radiologist to be limited by hardware artifact. Under the plan's own stated revision criteria, "pseudarthrosis" is an independent qualifying indication for revision surgery, separate from "hardware failure." Furthermore, the member has fully satisfied all standard medical necessity criteria under HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, and the denial violates California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5 regarding physical therapy prerequisites.

II. CLINICAL PRESENTATION AND HISTORY
Mr. George Harris is a 48-year-old male with a history of a prior C5-C6 ACDF performed in 2021, which initially yielded a good outcome. However, his symptoms recurred approximately 18 months postoperatively and have progressively worsened.
- Neurological Examination (September 20, 2024): Demonstrates a return of right C6 radicular symptoms, including 4/5 right bicep weakness, a diminished right bicep reflex, and C6 dermatomal numbness. These objective deficits are worse than his preoperative baseline from 2021.
- Imaging Studies:
  1. Cervical MRI (September 1, 2024): Demonstrated hardware artifact that limited the assessment. The radiologist noted a "possible non-union at C5-C6 but cannot confirm" and that "residual disc material or recurrent herniation cannot be excluded."
  2. Cervical CT Scan (September 15, 2024): Performed specifically to overcome the hardware artifact of the MRI. The CT scan confirmed "incomplete bridging bone formation" and "lucency around hardware suggesting pseudarthrosis." The radiologist concluded that the findings are "consistent with failed fusion/pseudarthrosis" and noted that the hardware itself appeared intact without fracture.
- Conservative Treatment:
  1. Physical Therapy: Completed 8 weeks (24 sessions) of supervised physical therapy. The treating therapist and physician noted no improvement and documented that physical therapy cannot address structural hardware or fusion failure.
  2. Pharmacotherapy: Completed a 4-month trial of Naproxen 500mg BID (NSAID) and a 3-month trial of Gabapentin 300mg TID (neuropathic agent), both resulting in only partial, inadequate relief.
  3. Interventional Treatment: Received a cervical epidural steroid injection on October 10, 2024, which resulted in minimal improvement, as expected in the presence of structural fusion failure.

III. PLAN CRITERIA COMPLIANCE ANALYSIS (CC-SPINE-2024)
The requested procedure (CPT 22551) fully satisfies the medical necessity criteria outlined in HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2:
1. Section 2.1 (Diagnosis Requirement): Mr. Harris has a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy, characterized by objective nerve root compression with radicular symptoms (right bicep weakness 4/5, diminished right bicep reflex, and C6 dermatomal numbness). This is supported by the CT scan dated September 15, 2024, demonstrating structural pathology (pseudarthrosis) consistent with his symptoms, satisfying the 6-month imaging window.
2. Section 2.2 (Conservative Treatment Requirement):
   - Section 2.2(a) (Physical Therapy): Mr. Harris completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (exceeding the 6-week minimum).
   - Section 2.2(b) (Pharmacotherapy): Mr. Harris completed trials of two qualifying agents for more than 4 weeks each: Naproxen (NSAID) for 4 months and Gabapentin (neuropathic agent) for 3 months.
   - Section 2.2(c) (Interventional Treatment): Mr. Harris received a cervical epidural steroid injection on October 10, 2024.
3. Section 2.3 (Imaging Requirement): The cervical CT scan dated September 15, 2024, is current (within 6 months) and demonstrates structural pathology (pseudarthrosis/failed fusion) at the proposed surgical level (C5-C6) consistent with his right C6 radiculopathy.
4. Section 2.4 (Physician Documentation): Dr. Karen Williams, MD, provided the required clinical documentation, including attestation of completed conservative treatment, clinical rationale for revision surgery, description of functional limitations, and discussion of surgical risks.

IV. RESOLUTION OF REVISION CRITERIA AND INITIAL DENIAL ERROR
The initial denial letter dated October 30, 2024, stated that "Revision criteria require documentation of hardware failure, pseudarthrosis, or new pathology... Documentation submitted does not confirm hardware failure."

This rationale contains a critical logical and clinical error:
1. Misapplication of Disjunctive Criteria: The plan's revision criteria, as quoted in the denial, are disjunctive ("hardware failure, pseudarthrosis, OR new pathology"). This means satisfying any one of these three conditions is sufficient. By denying the request solely because "hardware failure" was not confirmed, the plan reviewer ignored the other two criteria.
2. Failure to Review the Appropriate Imaging Modality: The cervical CT scan dated September 15, 2024, explicitly confirms "incomplete bridging bone formation" and "lucency around hardware," which are diagnostic of pseudarthrosis (failed fusion). The initial reviewer's reliance on the MRI report (which was limited by hardware artifact and could not confirm fusion status) to deny the request constitutes a serious clinical oversight. In the presence of spinal hardware, a CT scan is the clinically accepted gold standard for evaluating fusion status, as MRI is inherently limited by metallic artifact.

Because pseudarthrosis is documented on the CT scan, the member meets the plan's revision criteria.

V. CALIFORNIA REGULATORY COMPLIANCE ANALYSIS
Under California law, the plan's initial denial is non-compliant and must be overturned based on the following statutory provisions:
1. California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b) (Defective Denial Notice): A denial notice must specify the clinical criteria applied and the specific clinical reason for the denial. The plan's denial notice was procedurally defective because it misapplied the criteria by requiring "hardware failure" while ignoring the documented "pseudarthrosis," which is an independent qualifying criterion.
2. California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy as Prerequisite): Under CIC § 10169.5(a)(3), a health plan shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy where the condition involves objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address. Mr. Harris has objective structural compromise (pseudarthrosis with 4/5 bicep weakness and diminished reflex) that physical therapy cannot structurally repair. Furthermore, under CIC § 10169.5(a)(2), Mr. Harris completed 8 weeks of physical therapy and reached a documented functional plateau. Mechanically applying or extending physical therapy requirements in this clinical scenario violates California law.
3. CHSC § 1374.32 (Independent Medical Review Standard): Under California's IMR standard, "medically necessary" means services that a provider, exercising prudent clinical judgment, would provide in accordance with generally accepted standards of medical practice. CHSC § 1374.32(b) explicitly states that the IMR standard does not require consistency with the plan's internal coverage criteria. If this case were to proceed to an Independent Medical Review (IMR), the plan's denial would be overturned because revision surgery for symptomatic pseudarthrosis with objective neurological deficits is the standard of care.

VI. CLINICAL EVIDENCE AND GUIDELINES ANALYSIS
Generally accepted clinical standards strongly support revision surgery for Mr. Harris's presentation:
1. AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023): Revision surgery is indicated for symptomatic pseudarthrosis (failed fusion) with persistent radiculopathy and objective neurological deficits (Tier 1/Tier 2 indication). Mr. Harris exhibits progressive right C6 radiculopathy with objective motor weakness (4/5 bicep strength) and reflex changes.
2. NASS Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020): Support surgical intervention when conservative measures fail to address symptomatic non-union or pseudarthrosis. Mr. Harris has failed a comprehensive 8-week course of physical therapy, multiple pharmacotherapies, and an epidural steroid injection.
3. Imaging Standards: As outlined in the clinical reference summary, CT imaging is the appropriate and superior modality for assessing fusion status in patients with existing spinal hardware, as MRI is heavily limited by metallic artifact. The plan's reliance on the MRI to deny the request is contrary to standard radiological and neurosurgical practice.

VII. FINAL DETERMINATION
Based on the clinical record, HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, California statutory requirements (CHSC § 1374.31, CIC § 10169.5), and generally accepted clinical guidelines (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020), the prior authorization denial for Revision ACDF C5-C6 (CPT 22551) is OVERTURNED.

The requested procedure is medically necessary and is hereby APPROVED.

Member claims 8 total weeks but second provider (Mountain PT) records not received by plan. Cannot verify claimed treatment without complete records." (Reason Code: MED-003)

---

**SUMMARY OF APPEAL BASIS:**

The member's representative submitted an appeal stating that records from Mountain PT, documenting an additional 4 weeks of physical therapy, were enclosed. This brings the total completed physical therapy to 8 weeks across two providers. It was further noted that these records may have been submitted with the initial request but not received by the plan's initial reviewer.

---

**REVIEWER'S DETERMINATION:**

**OVERTURN**

---

**WARRANT (Detailed Rationale for Determination):**

Upon comprehensive review of the submitted appeal, the member's clinical record, HealthFirst's clinical coverage criteria (CC-SPINE-2024), California regulatory requirements, and generally accepted clinical standards, the denial for CPT code 22551 (ACDF C6-C7) is **OVERTURNED**.

**1. Clinical Presentation and Diagnosis:**
The member, Dorothy James, is presenting with a confirmed diagnosis of **bilateral cervical radiculopathy at C6-C7**.
*   **Imaging (MRI 2024-09-01):** Demonstrates a large disc herniation at C6-C7 with bilateral C7 nerve root compression and bilateral foraminal stenosis. Importantly, the MRI notes "mild cord contact without compression," and there is no mention of myelomalacia (cord signal change).
*   **Neurological Exam (2024-09-05):** Reveals bilateral C7 dermatomal symptoms, including bilateral tricep weakness (4/5), bilateral diminished tricep reflex, and bilateral finger tingling.
*   **Differentiation:** While bilateral symptoms are present, the absence of objective spinal cord compression, upper motor neuron signs (such as hyperreflexia, Hoffman's sign, clonus, or gait disturbance), and myelomalacia on MRI confirms that the primary diagnosis is severe bilateral radiculopathy, not cervical myelopathy. This distinction is critical for applying appropriate treatment guidelines, as the plan's myelopathy exception (Section 2.2(A)) and specific DMHC APL guidance for myelopathy with myelomalacia (DMHC APL 22-014, II.1) do not fully apply as the primary justification for this case.

**2. Review of HealthFirst Plan Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024):**
*   **2.1 Diagnosis Requirement:** The member meets criteria 2.1(a) (Cervical radiculopathy with radicular symptoms) and 2.1(c) (Cervical disc herniation with objective neurological deficit).
*   **2.2 Conservative Treatment Requirement:**
    *   **(b) Pharmacotherapy:** The member completed a trial of Pregabalin (3 months) and Naproxen (2 months), exceeding the 4-week minimum for two agents. **Criterion Met.**
    *   **(c) Interventional Treatment:** The member underwent a bilateral C7 epidural steroid injection. **Criterion Met.**
    *   **(a) Physical Therapy (PT):** The original denial cited "Physical therapy requirement not met" based on documentation of only 4 weeks of treatment. However, with the appeal, complete records from both Valley Physical Therapy (4 weeks) and Mountain Physical Therapy (4 weeks) are now provided, documenting a **total of 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy**. This *exceeds* the HealthFirst Plan Criteria requirement for a "minimum 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy" (CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2(a)).
        *   Furthermore, the PT records from Valley PT noted "Moderate improvement then plateau," and Mountain PT documented "No improvement in neurological symptoms. Plateau documented by PT at discharge." The plan's own criteria define "functional plateau" as "<10% improvement over 3 sessions OR therapist documents maximum benefit reached." The member clearly meets this definition, having completed 8 weeks of therapy with documented plateau and no improvement in neurological symptoms.

**3. Application of California Regulatory Requirements (State Law):**
*   **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy as Prerequisite):** This state law explicitly limits a plan's ability to condition surgical approval on physical therapy. Section 10169.5(a)(2) states that a health insurer "shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on completion of physical therapy where... The member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms."
    *   In this case, the member completed 8 weeks of physical therapy, and a functional plateau was clearly documented by the physical therapists. Therefore, the plan cannot deny the request based on the physical therapy requirement. This state law provision overrides any mechanical application of the plan's PT duration requirement, especially when a plateau has been achieved.

**4. Application of Clinical Standards (AANS/CNS, NASS, AO Spine Guidelines):**
*   **Surgical Indications:** According to AANS/CNS Joint Section on Disorders of the Spine Guidelines (2023 Update), NASS Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020), and AO Spine International Clinical Practice Guidelines (2021), surgery is strongly indicated (Tier 1) for patients with progressive neurological deficits despite conservative treatment or reasonably indicated (Tier 2) for radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks of conservative treatment and significant functional impairment.
*   **Adequacy of Conservative Trial:** The member has undergone an extensive conservative treatment course including 8 weeks of physical therapy with documented plateau, two pharmacotherapy agents for appropriate durations (Pregabalin for 3 months, Naproxen for 2 months), and an interventional C7 epidural injection with only temporary and partial relief returning to baseline. Given the persistent objective neurological deficits (bilateral C7 weakness 4/5, diminished reflex) despite these measures, the clinical standard supports surgical intervention.

**5. Resolution of Conflicts (Hierarchy: State Law > Clinical Standard > Plan Criteria):**
The initial denial was based on a lack of complete physical therapy records. With the submission of these records, the member has not only met but exceeded the plan's 6-week minimum PT duration requirement (completing 8 weeks). More critically, California state law (CIC § 10169.5) explicitly prohibits denial based on PT requirements when a functional plateau has been reached, which is clearly documented in this case. The patient's clinical presentation and documented failure of comprehensive conservative management align with generally accepted clinical standards for surgical intervention.

Therefore, based on the complete documentation provided, the plan's own criteria (with the new information), and the overriding authority of California state law, the basis for the initial denial is no longer valid. The requested ACDF C6-C7 is medically necessary and should be approved.

---

**NEXT STEPS:**

This determination to OVERTURN the denial means that the requested procedure, ACDF C6-C7, is approved. HealthFirst will process the authorization for the service.

The member retains the right to an Independent Medical Review (IMR) through the California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) if they disagree with any aspect of this appeal determination. Information about IMR is available on the DMHC website or by calling 1-888-HMO-2219.

**BACKGROUND:**
Mr. Steven Clark, a 46-year-old member of HealthFirst PPO Gold, was denied prior authorization for an Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6. The initial denial (MED-003) cited conflicting physical therapy documentation, stating uncertainty regarding the total duration of PT completed and that the plan required verification of PT duration before approval. The member's appeal asserts that both sets of PT records (Riverside PT and Coastal PT) are authentic, the discrepancy was due to incomplete initial submission for Coastal PT, and complete records demonstrating 6 weeks from each provider (12 weeks total) are now enclosed.

**CLINICAL PRESENTATION & DIAGNOSIS:**
The clinical record indicates a presenting diagnosis of Cervical Radiculopathy C5-C6 with functional impairment.
*   **Imaging (MRI 2024-08-15):** Revealed a C5-C6 large disc herniation with severe right C6 nerve root compression and foraminal stenosis. No evidence of myelomalacia or spinal cord compression was reported, consistent with radiculopathy rather than myelopathy.
*   **Neurological Exam (2024-08-20):** Demonstrated right C6 dermatomal numbness, bicep weakness 4/5 right, absent right bicep reflex, and a positive Spurling sign on the right. These findings are consistent with C6 radiculopathy. No upper motor neuron signs suggestive of myelopathy were documented.

**CONSERVATIVE TREATMENT HISTORY:**
*   **Physical Therapy:**
    *   Riverside Physical Therapy: 6 weeks (April 1 - May 10, 2024), 18 sessions. Records received complete. Documented "Plateau. Symptoms persist."
    *   Coastal Physical Therapy: 6 weeks (June 1 - July 12, 2024), 18 sessions. Complete records now submitted, initial submission was partial. Documented "No improvement in neurological deficit. Therapist documents functional plateau — maximum therapeutic benefit reached."
    *   **Total PT:** 12 weeks, 36 sessions. All records are now complete and verified.
*   **Pharmacotherapy:**
    *   Gabapentin 600mg TID for 5 months, with partial relief.
    *   Duloxetine 60mg daily for 3 months, with partial neuropathic benefit.
*   **Interventional Treatment:**
    *   Right C6 epidural steroid injection (August 28, 2024), providing 60% temporary relief, with symptoms returning to baseline within 3 weeks.

**REVIEW OF PLAN CRITERIA (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024):**

1.  **2.1 Diagnosis Requirement:** Member has a confirmed diagnosis of Cervical Radiculopathy with objective nerve root compression on MRI and correlating radicular symptoms/neurological deficits. **MET.**
2.  **2.2 Conservative Treatment Requirement:**
    *   **(a) Physical therapy:** Minimum 6 weeks of supervised PT with documented functional outcomes. The member completed 12 weeks of PT with two separate providers, both documenting a functional plateau and persistent symptoms/neurological deficits. **MET.**
    *   **(b) Pharmacotherapy:** Trial of at least two agents for minimum 4 weeks each. The member completed trials of Gabapentin (5 months) and Duloxetine (3 months). **MET.**
    *   **(c) Interventional Treatment:** One interventional treatment. The member received a right C6 epidural steroid injection. **MET.**
    *   *Myelopathy Exception 2.2(A):* This exception is not applicable as the primary diagnosis is cervical radiculopathy, not myelopathy.
3.  **2.3 Imaging Requirement:** Current MRI (within 6 months) demonstrates structural pathology (C5-C6 disc herniation, severe right C6 nerve root compression, foraminal stenosis) consistent with symptoms and proposed surgical level. **MET.**
4.  **2.4 Physician Documentation:** While specific attestations are not provided in the submitted summary, the request for surgery implies the treating physician's rationale, and functional limitations (bicep weakness) are documented.

**Conclusion on Plan Criteria:** The member has met all of HealthFirst's Medical Necessity Criteria for ACDF for cervical radiculopathy. The initial denial basis (conflicting PT documentation) has been fully resolved by the appeal.

**REVIEW OF CALIFORNIA REGULATORY FRAMEWORK:**

1.  **CIC § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy as Prerequisite):**
    *   This statute dictates that a plan shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on completion of physical therapy where:
        *   (a)(2) "The member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms." The member completed 12 weeks of PT, and both PT providers explicitly documented functional plateau and persistent neurological deficits. This condition is **MET**.
        *   (a)(3) "The condition involves objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address." The MRI demonstrates severe C6 nerve root compression, and the neurological exam confirms objective bicep weakness (4/5) and absent reflex. This constitutes objective structural neurological compromise. This condition is **MET**.
    *   Therefore, even if the plan's PT requirement was at issue (which it is not, as 12 weeks were completed), state law would prevent denial based on this factor.
2.  **DMHC APL 22-014 (Myelopathy and Urgent Conditions):**
    *   While primarily focused on myelopathy, Section II.3 states: "Plans shall not apply internal criteria that are more restrictive than generally accepted standards of medical practice... Where a conflict exists between plan criteria and generally accepted standards, the clinical standard governs." This reinforces the need to consider generally accepted standards of care.
3.  **CHSC § 1374.32(b) (Standard of Review for IMR):**
    *   This section, applicable to IMR, specifies that medical necessity is determined by "generally accepted standards of medical practice," not solely by the plan's internal criteria. This principle implies that care consistent with clinical standards should be approved.

**Conclusion on State Law:** California state law strongly supports the approval of this request, particularly given the documented functional plateau from conservative treatment and objective neurological compromise.

**REVIEW OF CLINICAL STANDARD (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020, AO Spine 2021):**

1.  **Diagnostic Classification (Section 1.1):** The member's presentation clearly aligns with Cervical Radiculopathy: compression of an individual nerve root (C6), unilateral symptoms (right C6 dermatomal numbness, bicep weakness, absent reflex), and absence of upper motor neuron signs.
2.  **Conservative Treatment Duration (Section 2.1, 2.2, Summary Table):** For radiculopathy, clinical guidelines support a trial of 6-12 weeks of conservative treatment. The member completed an extensive 12-week course of PT, alongside pharmacotherapy and interventional procedures, all with documented lack of sustained improvement and a functional plateau.
3.  **Functional Plateau Definition (Section 5):** The clinical standard defines functional plateau as "therapist documentation that patient has reached maximum therapeutic benefit" or "no improvement in neurological symptoms (weakness, reflex changes) after 6-8 weeks of PT." Both PT providers documented a functional plateau, and the member continues to exhibit objective bicep weakness (4/5) and an absent reflex after 12 weeks of PT.
4.  **Surgical Indications (Section 3.1):** Per AANS/CNS guidelines, surgery is a reasonable option (Tier 2) for "Radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks conservative tx" and "Significant functional impairment not responding to conservative care." The member meets both of these criteria.

**Conclusion on Clinical Standard:** The requested ACDF is consistent with generally accepted standards of medical practice for cervical radiculopathy, given the severe nerve root compression, objective neurological deficit, and failure of an extensive course of conservative treatment with documented functional plateau.

**CONFLICT RESOLUTION AND FINAL DETERMINATION:**
The initial denial was based on a documentation issue that has been fully resolved by the appeal. Upon review of the complete clinical record, it is evident that the member has fulfilled and exceeded HealthFirst's own criteria for conservative treatment for cervical radiculopathy, including 12 weeks of physical therapy, two pharmacotherapy agents, and one interventional procedure, all with documented inadequate response and functional plateau.

Furthermore, California state law (CIC § 10169.5) explicitly prohibits plans from denying surgical approval based on physical therapy requirements when a functional plateau has been reached and objective structural neurological compromise exists, both of which are present in this case. The requested ACDF is also fully supported by generally accepted clinical standards of medical practice for cervical radiculopathy with persistent symptoms and objective neurological deficits after conservative treatment failure.

There are no conflicts among the three sources of authority; all support the approval of the requested procedure.

**DISPOSITION:** OVERTURN

**WARRANT:**
The denial for prior authorization of ACDF C5-C6 is **OVERTURNED**. The appeal successfully addressed the original denial reason by providing complete and verified physical therapy documentation, demonstrating that the member completed 12 weeks of PT with documented functional plateaus from both providers. This duration significantly exceeds the HealthFirst plan's minimum 6-week PT requirement for radiculopathy. Additionally, the member has completed trials of two pharmacotherapy agents (Gabapentin for 5 months, Duloxetine for 3 months) and one interventional procedure (right C6 epidural with temporary relief), all with persistent objective neurological deficits (right C6 dermatomal numbness, bicep weakness 4/5, absent bicep reflex) and functional impairment.

The clinical presentation, characterized by severe right C6 nerve root compression on MRI and correlating neurological deficits, fully meets the criteria for surgical intervention for cervical radiculopathy under HealthFirst's own Clinical Coverage Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024, Sections 2.1(a), 2.2(a,b,c), 2.3). Moreover, California Insurance Code § 10169.5 (a)(2) and (a)(3) explicitly state that a plan cannot condition surgical approval on further PT when a functional plateau has been reached or when there is objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that PT cannot address, both conditions being met in this case. Finally, the requested ACDF is consistent with generally accepted standards of medical practice for cervical radiculopathy with objective neurological deficits unresponsive to an adequate trial of conservative management, as outlined in AANS/CNS, NASS, and AO Spine guidelines.

**Citations:**
*   HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.1(a), 2.2(a), 2.2(b), 2.2(c), 2.3.
*   California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5 (a)(2), (a)(3).
*   AANS/CNS Joint Section on Disorders of the Spine: Guidelines for Management of Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (2023 Update), Section 3.1 Tier 2(b,c), Section 5 Functional Plateau Definition.
*   North American Spine Society (NASS): Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020), Section 2.1.
*   AO Spine International: Clinical Practice Guideline (2021), Section 2.1.

**State of California — Department of Managed Health Care / Department of Insurance**  
**Independent Medical Review & Clinical Appeals Division**

---

### FORMAL APPEAL DETERMINATION

| **Case Information** | **Details** |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Case ID** | PA-2024-F001 |
| **Member Name** | Dorothy James |

| **Plan Year** | 2024 |
| **Requested Procedure** | Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C6-C7, single level (CPT 22551) |
| **Requesting Physician** | Dr. Paul Adams, MD — Spine Surgery |
| **Facility** | UCLA Medical Center |
| **Initial Denial Date** | November 2, 2024 |
| **Initial Reviewer** | Dr. Alan Foster, MD (Initial Denial Reason: MED-003) |
| **Appeal Filed Date** | November 12, 2024 |

---

### FORMAL DISPOSITION
Pursuant to the California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32(b) and California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5, the initial determination by HealthFirst to deny authorization for CPT 22551 (ACDF C6-C7) is hereby **OVERTURNED**. 

The requested surgical procedure is **APPROVED** as medically necessary. HealthFirst shall authorize the procedure at UCLA Medical Center under Dr. Paul Adams, MD, with an authorization validity window of 90 days from the date of this order.

---

### CLINICAL RECORD SUMMARY

1. **Presenting Clinical Picture**: 51-year-old female presenting with a history of progressive, bilateral C7 cervical radiculopathy. 
2. **Neurological Examination (September 5, 2024)**: 
   * Bilateral C7 dermatomal symptoms.
   * Objective motor deficit: Bilateral tricep weakness rated at 4/5.
   * Reflexes: Bilateral tricep reflexes are diminished (lower motor neuron sign).
   * Sensory: Bilateral finger tingling in the C7 distribution.
   * Gait and coordination: Normal (no signs of myelopathic gait or upper motor neuron signs).
3. **Diagnostic Imaging (MRI Cervical Spine, September 1, 2024)**:
   * Demonstration of a large C6-C7 disc herniation.
   * Bilateral C7 nerve root compression.
   * Bilateral foraminal stenosis.
   * Mild spinal cord contact *without* compression or signal change (no myelomalacia).
4. **Conservative Treatment History**:
   * **Physical Therapy (PT)**: 
     * *Provider 1 (Valley PT)*: June 1, 2024 – June 28, 2024 (4 weeks, 12 sessions). Documented moderate initial improvement followed by a clinical plateau.
     * *Provider 2 (Mountain PT)*: July 15, 2024 – August 9, 2024 (4 weeks, 12 sessions). Submitted on appeal. Documented no improvement in neurological symptoms with a confirmed functional plateau at discharge.
     * *Cumulative PT*: 8 total weeks, 24 sessions.
   * **Pharmacotherapy**: 
     * Pregabalin 150mg BID for 3 months (neuropathic agent; achieved partial temporary relief).
     * Naproxen 500mg BID for 2 months (NSAID; inadequate response).
   * **Interventional Therapy**:
     * Bilateral C7 epidural steroid injection on September 20, 2024, resulting in transient relief (50% relief on the left, 30% on the right) with a rapid return to baseline symptoms.

---

### STEP-BY-STEP EVALUATION ANALYSIS

#### Step 1: Procedural Adequacy and Defect Check (CHSC § 1374.31(b))
The plan’s initial denial notice dated November 2, 2024, cited reason code MED-003, stating that the required 6-week conservative physical therapy course could not be verified because only 4 weeks of records (Valley PT) were in the plan's possession. 
* **Finding**: The initial denial was **procedurally adequate** at the time of issue. It specified the criteria applied (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2), provided an individualized clinical rationale (inability to verify the second 4-week block of therapy at Mountain PT), and notified the member of appeal and IMR rights. No procedural defect exists; the denial was based on an administrative record deficiency that has now been resolved on appeal.

#### Step 2: Diagnostic and Pathology Classification
The clinical findings and diagnostic imaging must be classified to determine the appropriate treatment pathway (Radiculopathy vs. Myelopathy).
* **Finding**: The member's primary pathology is classified as **Bilateral Cervical Radiculopathy (C6-C7)**. 
* **Clinical Rationale**: The neurological exam confirms lower motor neuron pathology (diminished tricep reflexes, 4/5 tricep weakness, dermatomal tingling). The MRI confirms bilateral C7 nerve root compression from a large C6-C7 herniation. While the MRI notes "mild cord contact," it explicitly states there is "no compression" and no T2-weighted cord signal changes (myelomalacia). Additionally, there are no upper motor neuron signs (such as hyperreflexia, Hoffman's sign, clonus, or gait disturbance) to support a diagnosis of cervical myelopathy. Therefore, the myelopathy exceptions do not apply, and the case must be evaluated under the standard Radiculopathy pathway.

#### Step 3: Statutory Override Analysis (California Law)
Under California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5, health plans are restricted from mechanically enforcing rigid physical therapy duration requirements under specified conditions.
* **Finding**: **A statutory override applies under CIC § 10169.5(a)(2).** 
* **Statutory Rationale**: The statute states that a plan shall not condition surgical approval on the completion of further physical therapy if the member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating clinician/therapist documents that the member reached a "functional plateau" without adequate resolution of symptoms. 
* In this case, the member completed a cumulative 8 weeks (24 sessions) of physical therapy across two facilities. The discharge records from Mountain PT (submitted with this appeal) and Valley PT both document that the member reached a clear functional plateau with persistent, objective neurological deficits (4/5 motor weakness). Under CIC § 10169.5(c), the plan's mechanical application of a 6-week continuous single-provider requirement is legally overridden by the documented 8-week multi-provider trial and resulting clinical plateau.

#### Step 4: Plan Criteria Compliance Evaluation (CC-SPINE-2024)
Because the primary diagnosis is cervical radiculopathy, compliance must be measured against the standard requirements of HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2:

* **Section 2.1 (Diagnosis)**: **MET**. Bilateral C6-C7 radiculopathy is confirmed by clinical exam (tricep weakness, reflex loss) and correlating MRI showing a C6-C7 herniation with bilateral C7 nerve root compression within the 6-month window (September 1, 2024).
* **Section 2.2(a) (Physical Therapy)**: **MET**. The criteria require a minimum of 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy. With the submission of the Mountain PT records (4 weeks, July 15 – Aug 9, 2024) combined with the previously received Valley PT records (4 weeks, June 1 – June 28, 2024), the member has documented **8 weeks** of supervised cervical PT, exceeding the plan's 6-week requirement.
* **Section 2.2(b) (Pharmacotherapy)**: **MET**. Documentation confirms trials of two qualifying agents for a minimum of 4 weeks each: Pregabalin (neuropathic, 3 months) and Naproxen (NSAID, 2 months).
* **Section 2.2(c) (Interventional)**: **MET**. The member underwent a bilateral C7 epidural steroid injection on September 20, 2024, providing only short-term temporary relief before returning to baseline.
* **Section 2.3 & 2.4 (Imaging & Documentation)**: **MET**. MRI is current within 6 months, and Dr. Adams provided the necessary surgical risk/benefit counseling and clinical justifications.

* **Conclusion**: The member now satisfies **100% of the medical necessity criteria** outlined in HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024. The initial administrative reason for denial (lack of PT verification) has been fully resolved by the submitted appeal packet.

#### Step 5: Clinical Standard Evidentiary Review (CHSC § 1374.32(b))
Under California law, clinical review standards must align with generally accepted standards of medical practice, which supersede plan policies if the plan's criteria are more restrictive.
* **Finding**: The requested ACDF meets generally accepted standards of medical practice.
* **Clinical Rationale**: According to the joint guidelines of the American Association of Neurological Surgeons (AANS) and the Congress of Neurological Surgeons (AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines 2023), surgical decompression is highly indicated (Tier 1/2) for patients with cervical radiculopathy who present with objective neurological deficits (e.g., 4/5 motor weakness, diminished reflexes) and have failed a comprehensive 6- to 12-week trial of conservative therapy. 
* This clinical expectation is mirrored in the North American Spine Society (NASS) 2020 Guidelines. Forcing a patient with a structural disc herniation, persistent motor weakness, and a documented functional plateau to undergo further conservative management poses an unnecessary risk of permanent nerve root injury. The clinical standard mandates surgical decompression at this stage.

---

### CONCLUSION OF EVALUATION

Applying the governing **Hierarchy of Authority**:
$$\text{California State Law (CIC § 10169.5)} > \text{Generally Accepted Clinical Standards (AANS/CNS)} > \text{HealthPlan Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024)}$$

1. **State Law**: Prohibits the plan from denying the surgery on the basis of physical therapy requirements when a functional plateau has been reached and documented (which is established by the Mountain PT discharge summary).
2. **Clinical Standards**: Strongly recommend surgical intervention for cervical radiculopathy associated with motor weakness (4/5 triceps) that has failed 8 weeks of physical therapy, multiple pharmacotherapies, and an epidural injection.
3. **Plan Criteria**: Are fully satisfied under Section 2.2 once the Mountain PT records submitted with this appeal are combined with the Valley PT records to verify 8 weeks of total treatment.

Under all three tiers of the authority hierarchy, the requested single-level ACDF (C6-C7) is medically necessary and clinically appropriate. 

---

### DECISION AND ORDER
HealthFirst Health Plan is hereby ordered to **OVERTURN** its initial denial and **APPROVE** prior authorization request PA-2024-F001 for CPT code 22551 (ACDF C6-C7) at UCLA Medical Center, to be performed by Dr. Paul Adams, MD.

The initial denial dated October 10, 2024, was based on an administrative record discrepancy regarding the duration of physical therapy (PT) completed by the member. The plan’s initial reviewer noted a conflict between records submitted by Riverside PT (6 weeks) and Coastal PT (4 weeks), declaring the total duration "uncertain." 

Upon administrative and clinical review of the complete appeal packet, this denial is overturned on four independent, compounding grounds:
1. **Procedural Defect:** The initial denial notice was procedurally defective under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b) for failing to cite specific clinical coverage criteria.
2. **Statutory Override:** Under California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(2), the plan is legally prohibited from conditioning surgical approval on further physical therapy because the member has completed an extensive course of PT and reached a documented functional plateau.
3. **Plan Criteria Compliance:** The complete clinical records submitted with this appeal resolve all prior documentation discrepancies, establishing that the member has verified completion of 12 weeks of PT, 5 months of gabapentin, 3 months of duloxetine, and a cervical epidural steroid injection, thereby fully satisfying HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2.
4. **Clinical Standard Medical Necessity:** Under CHSC § 1374.32(b) and generally accepted clinical guidelines (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020), surgical intervention is medically necessary for a patient with persistent cervical radiculopathy, objective motor deficit (4/5 bicep weakness, absent reflex), and failed comprehensive conservative therapy.

---

## III. Step-by-Step Appeal Evaluation

### Step 1: Procedural Defect & Technical Adequacy Review (CHSC § 1374.31(b))
A threshold review of the plan’s initial denial notice dated October 10, 2024, reveals a fatal procedural defect under California regulatory standards:
* **Statutory Requirement:** CHSC § 1374.31(a)(2) mandates that any medical necessity denial notice *shall* explicitly specify the clinical criteria applied and the specific clinical reasoning supporting the denial.
* **Review of Initial Notice:** The initial denial notice (Reason Code: MED-003) stated: *"Conflicting physical therapy documentation... Records conflict on duration... Plan requires verification of claimed PT duration before approval."* The notice failed to cite the applicable coverage policy (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024) or the specific section (Section 2.2) being enforced. Furthermore, it did not connect the administrative document verification to any clinical medical necessity rationale.
* **Finding:** The denial notice is **procedurally defective** under CHSC § 1374.31(b). Under California law, a defective notice must be treated as if it were never issued for the purposes of timeline rules. This procedural failure constitutes immediate and sufficient grounds to **overturn** the denial.

### Step 2: Clinical Classification & Diagnostic Verification
To determine the correct clinical and regulatory pathway, the member's clinical presentation must be classified:
* **Myelopathy vs. Radiculopathy:** 
  * *Myelopathy* requires objective spinal cord compression on MRI, upper motor neuron (UMN) signs (hyperreflexia, Hoffman sign, gait disturbance), and bilateral deficits.
  * *Radiculopathy* is characterized by nerve root compression, unilateral dermatomal symptoms, and lower motor neuron signs (hyporeflexia, localized weakness).
* **Clinical Record Analysis:** 
  * **Imaging:** The MRI dated August 15, 2024, reveals a *C5-C6 large disc herniation with severe right C6 nerve root compression and foraminal stenosis*. No spinal cord compression or myelomalacia (cord signal change) is documented.
  * **Neurological Exam:** Objective findings dated August 20, 2024, show *right C6 dermatomal numbness, bicep weakness (4/5 right), and an absent bicep reflex (0/4 right)*, alongside a positive right Spurling's maneuver. 
* **Finding:** The member's primary diagnostic presentation is **Cervical Radiculopathy with objective neurological deficit**. There is no clinical or imaging evidence of cervical myelopathy. Therefore, standard radiculopathy algorithms and conservative treatment pathways apply.

### Step 3: State Statutory Override Analysis (CIC § 10169.5)
Under California Insurance Code § 10169.5, a health plan is legally prohibited from mechanically conditioning approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy if specific statutory exceptions are met:
* **Functional Plateau Standard (CIC § 10169.5(a)(2)):** Insurers cannot enforce PT requirements if the member has completed therapy and reached a "functional plateau" (defined as a failure to achieve meaningful clinical improvement, as documented by the physical therapist or physician).
* **Evidence in Appeal Record:**
  * **Riverside Physical Therapy:** Completed 6 weeks (18 sessions) from April 1, 2024, to May 10, 2024. The clinical outcome note explicitly states: *"Plateau documented. Symptoms persist."*
  * **Coastal Physical Therapy:** Completed 6 weeks (18 sessions) from June 1, 2024, to July 12, 2024. The complete records, now enclosed, verify the final 2 weeks of therapy and include an outcome note stating: *"No improvement in neurological deficit. Therapist documents functional plateau — maximum therapeutic benefit reached."*
* **Finding:** The member has completed a total of 12 weeks of supervised PT and reached a documented functional plateau at two independent facilities. Under CIC § 10169.5(a)(2), the plan's requirement for further physical therapy or further administrative "verification" of therapy duration is legally overridden.

### Step 4: Plan Criteria Compliance (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2)
Now that the complete Coastal PT records have been submitted, the documentation discrepancy is fully resolved. A clinical review against HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2 demonstrates 100% compliance:

| Policy Criteria (Section 2.2) | Member Clinical Data | Compliance Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **2.1 Diagnosis Requirement** | Confirmed C5-C6 disc herniation with severe C6 root compression & objective neurological deficit (4/5 right bicep weakness, absent right bicep reflex). | **MET** |
| **2.2(a) Physical Therapy** | Requires $\ge$ 6 weeks. Member completed **12 weeks total** (6 weeks Riverside PT, 6 weeks Coastal PT). | **MET** (Exceeded by 100%) |
| **2.2(b) Pharmacotherapy** | Requires trial of 2 agents for $\ge$ 4 weeks each. Member completed: (1) Gabapentin 600mg TID for 5 months, (2) Duloxetine 60mg daily for 3 months. | **MET** |
| **2.2(c) Interventional** | Requires at least 1 interventional procedure. Member received a right C6 epidural steroid injection on August 28, 2024 (resulted in 60% temporary relief, returned to baseline in 3 weeks). | **MET** |
| **2.3 Current Imaging** | MRI within 6 months showing correlating pathology. MRI dated August 15, 2024 shows severe right C6 nerve root compression matching right-sided bicep weakness and numbness. | **MET** |
| **2.4 Physician Documentation** | Dr. Nguyen provided clinical rationale, functional limitations, and surgical risk counseling. | **MET** |

* **Finding:** Every clinical and conservative criteria element under Section 2.2 of the plan's policy is fully met. The sole barrier to the initial authorization (unverifiable PT duration) has been thoroughly resolved with the submission of the complete Coastal PT records.

### Step 5: Clinical Standard Medical Necessity Review (AANS/CNS & NASS Guidelines)
Under California Health & Safety Code § 1374.32(b) (the IMR medical necessity standard), the clinical review must evaluate the request against generally accepted clinical standards of medical practice, which supersede restrictive internal plan criteria:
* **Clinical Standard of Care:** According to the North American Spine Society (NASS) 2020 Clinical Guidelines and the AANS/CNS Joint Section Guidelines (2023), surgical decompression and fusion (ACDF) is strongly indicated (Tier 1/2 Clinical Indication) for patients with cervical radiculopathy who present with:
  1. A correlating herniated disc on MRI compressing the nerve root.
  2. Objective, progressive, or persistent motor weakness (such as the member's 4/5 bicep weakness and absent reflex).
  3. Failure of a structured 6-to-12-week conservative management regimen (including physical therapy, neuropathic medications, and epidural steroid injections).
* **Risk of Delay:** Continued delay of surgical decompression in a patient with active motor weakness (4/5 bicep strength) and an absent reflex risks permanent, irreversible lower motor neuron injury and persistent muscle atrophy.
* **Finding:** Standard clinical medical guidelines confirm that C5-C6 ACDF is highly appropriate, medically necessary, and the definitive standard of care for Steven Clark. 

---

## IV. Final Directive & Instruction to Health Plan
Pursuant to California regulatory authority and the clinical evidence presented:
1. **HealthFirst Health Plan** shall immediately **OVERTURN** the initial denial.
2. The plan is directed to issue an approval authorization for **CPT Code 22551 (ACDF C5-C6, one level)** to be performed by Dr. Sarah Nguyen, MD at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center.

## HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN — PRIOR AUTHORIZATION APPEAL DETERMINATION

**Case ID:** PA-2024-G001
**Member:** Marco Reyes (M-G001), Age 49
**Procedure:** ACDF C6-C7, one level (CPT 22551)
**Requested By:** Dr. Sarah Okonkwo, MD
**Facility:** UCSF Medical Center
**Date of Appeal Review:** 2024-11-05
**Reviewer:** [Your Name/Title - Expert Appeals Reviewer]

---

### EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This appeal review concerns the denial of prior authorization for an Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C6-C7 for Mr. Marco Reyes. The initial denial was based on the claim that the member had completed only 3 weeks of physical therapy (PT) and had no documented functional plateau, thereby failing to meet conservative treatment requirements under HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2.

Upon review of the submitted clinical record and appeal basis, it is evident that the initial denial contained significant factual errors and misapplied the plan's own criteria. The member has completed 9 weeks of physical therapy, and a functional plateau is clearly documented. Furthermore, state law explicitly prohibits conditioning approval on further PT once a functional plateau is reached.

**Decision: OVERTURN DENIAL**

---

### BACKGROUND AND DENIAL REASON

Mr. Marco Reyes, a 49-year-old HealthFirst PPO Gold member, was denied prior authorization for an ACDF at C6-C7. The presenting diagnosis is persistent right-sided cervical radiculopathy at C6-C7.

The initial denial, issued on 2024-11-01 by Dr. Alan Foster, MD (HealthFirst Utilization Management), cited reason code MED-003, stating: "Member does not meet conservative treatment requirements under CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2. Physical therapy: member has completed only 3 weeks of physical therapy. Standard pathway requires 6 weeks minimum. Functional plateau not documented. All other criteria remain unmet."

The member's appeal asserts that the denial miscounts PT duration, that 9 weeks of PT were completed across two providers, that both records were submitted with the original request, that functional plateau was explicitly documented, and that all other conservative treatment criteria were met.

---

### CLINICAL RECORD SUMMARY

*   **Diagnosis:** Cervical radiculopathy C6-C7, right-sided, persistent.
*   **Imaging (MRI 2024-08-20):** Large C6-C7 disc herniation with moderate right C7 nerve root compression. **No cord contact. No myelomalacia.** Right foraminal stenosis confirmed.
*   **Neurological Exam (2024-08-25):** Right C7 dermatomal numbness, diminished right triceps reflex, 4/5 right grip strength. **No bilateral findings. No Upper Motor Neuron (UMN) signs.**
*   **Conservative Treatment:**
    *   **Physical Therapy:**
        *   Valley PT: 3 weeks (2024-06-01 to 2024-06-21), 9 sessions. Outcome: Partial improvement, symptoms persist.
        *   Capital PT: 6 weeks (2024-07-08 to 2024-08-16), 18 sessions. Outcome: Functional plateau reached. Discharge summary explicitly states: "Maximum therapeutic benefit achieved. No further improvement expected from continued PT."
        *   **Total PT:** 9 weeks, 27 sessions. All records submitted with original PA request.
    *   **Pharmacotherapy:** Gabapentin 600mg TID for 4 months (partial relief); Naproxen 500mg BID for 3 months (inadequate).
    *   **Interventional:** Right C7 epidural steroid injection (2024-09-15). Response: 35% temporary relief, returned to baseline in 3 weeks.

---

### REVIEW AND ANALYSIS

The appeal was reviewed using the established hierarchy: State law > Clinical standard > Plan criteria.

**1. Primary Clinical Presentation:**
Based on the clinical record, the member's diagnosis is unequivocally **Cervical Radiculopathy**. The MRI explicitly notes "No cord contact. No myelomalacia," and the neurological exam states "No bilateral findings. No UMN signs." This distinction is critical as it determines the applicable treatment pathway and conservative treatment requirements. Therefore, the myelopathy exception in CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2(A) and related myelopathy-specific guidance (e.g., DMHC APL 22-014 regarding myelomalacia) are not directly applicable to the diagnosis itself, but the general principles of appropriate conservative care, factual accuracy, and state law apply.

**2. Application of HealthFirst Plan Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024):**
The initial denial incorrectly claimed the member completed only 3 weeks of PT and that functional plateau was not documented.
*   **Section 2.2(a) Physical Therapy:** The plan requires a "minimum 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy with documented functional outcomes."
    *   The member completed a total of **9 weeks** of physical therapy across two providers, exceeding the 6-week minimum. (Clinical Record: physical_therapy_summary, authoritative_source: structured_fields_in_this_record).
    *   A functional plateau was explicitly documented in the Capital PT discharge summary: "Maximum therapeutic benefit achieved. No further improvement expected from continued PT." (Clinical Record: physical_therapy_provider_2, physical_therapy_summary).
    *   Therefore, the member **fully met** the physical therapy requirement under the plan's standard pathway.
*   **Section 2.2(b) Pharmacotherapy:** The plan requires "at least two... for minimum 4 weeks each."
    *   Gabapentin was used for 4 months. Naproxen was used for 3 months. (Clinical Record: pharmacotherapy).
    *   This criterion is **met**.
*   **Section 2.2(c) Interventional Treatment:** The plan requires "one of the following."
    *   The member underwent a Right C7 epidural steroid injection. (Clinical Record: interventional).
    *   This criterion is **met**.
*   **Section 2.1 Diagnosis & 2.3 Imaging:** These criteria are also **met**, as confirmed by the MRI findings of C6-C7 disc herniation with C7 nerve root compression correlating with the clinical presentation of cervical radiculopathy.

**Conclusion on Plan Criteria:** The member fully meets HealthFirst's own criteria for surgical authorization, including all conservative treatment requirements. The denial was based on demonstrably false factual claims regarding the duration of PT and documentation of functional plateau.

**3. Application of California Regulatory Requirements:**
*   **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy as Prerequisite):** This state law explicitly states that a health insurer cannot condition approval of a surgical procedure on completion of physical therapy where: "(2) The member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms; OR (3) The condition involves objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address."
    *   Mr. Reyes meets provision (2): he completed 9 weeks of PT, and his physical therapist explicitly documented a functional plateau with persistent symptoms. This state law **mandates approval** regardless of any plan-imposed minimum PT duration beyond the documented plateau. (Source: California Regulatory Framework, Part III).
*   **California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b) (Denial Notice Defective):** A denial notice that relies on factually incorrect information to determine criteria are not met is substantively flawed. While the denial *cited* criteria, its factual basis for non-compliance was erroneous.
*   **DMHC APL 22-014 (Myelopathy and Urgent Conditions):** While this APL focuses on myelopathy, it reinforces the principle that plans shall not apply internal criteria that are more restrictive than generally accepted standards. In this case, the plan's misapplication of its own criteria, leading to a denial despite criteria being met and a functional plateau documented, is contrary to the spirit of appropriate medical necessity review.

**4. Application of Clinical Standard (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020, AO Spine 2021):**
*   For cervical radiculopathy, generally accepted clinical guidelines (e.g., AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines 2023, Section 3.1 Tier 2) indicate surgery as a "reasonable option" for "Radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks conservative tx."
*   Mr. Reyes has undergone 9 weeks of PT (within the 6-12 week range), two pharmacotherapy agents for 3-4 months, and one epidural injection with only temporary, partial relief. His symptoms (numbness, diminished reflex, weakness) persist.
*   The clinical definition of a functional plateau includes "Therapist documentation that patient has reached maximum therapeutic benefit." (Clinical Reference Summary, Section 5). This is consistent with the Capital PT discharge summary.
*   Therefore, the requested ACDF for persistent radiculopathy after a comprehensive trial of conservative treatment is **medically necessary and consistent with generally accepted standards of medical practice.**

**5. Conflict Resolution:**
The initial denial directly contradicts the facts documented in the clinical record and the provisions of state law (CIC § 10169.5). The plan's criteria for conservative treatment, when correctly applied to the actual clinical evidence, are also met. Furthermore, the requested service aligns with established clinical guidelines for persistent cervical radiculopathy.

---

### CONCLUSION

The initial denial of prior authorization for Mr. Marco Reyes's ACDF C6-C7 was based on demonstrably incorrect factual information regarding the duration of physical therapy and the documentation of a functional plateau. The member has completed 9 weeks of physical therapy and a functional plateau was explicitly documented by his therapist. He has also met all other conservative treatment requirements outlined in the HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024 policy.

Furthermore, California law (CIC § 10169.5) prohibits plans from denying surgery based on a minimum PT duration once a functional plateau has been reached. The requested procedure is also consistent with generally accepted clinical standards for persistent cervical radiculopathy after failed conservative management.

Therefore, the criteria for medical necessity have been met under the plan's own policy, state law, and generally accepted clinical standards.

---

### DISPOSITION

**OVERTURN DENIAL.**

The prior authorization for ACDF C6-C7 (CPT 22551) for Mr. Marco Reyes is **APPROVED**.

---

**Warrant:** The denial is overturned because:
1.  **Factual Error:** The initial denial was based on a factual error, incorrectly stating the member completed only 3 weeks of physical therapy and that functional plateau was not documented. The clinical record clearly shows 9 weeks of PT completed and explicit documentation of functional plateau. (Clinical Record: conservative_treatment, physical_therapy_summary).
2.  **Plan Criteria Met:** The member fully met HealthFirst's own conservative treatment requirements under CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2 (9 weeks PT > 6-week minimum, documented functional plateau, 2 pharmacotherapy agents > 4 weeks, 1 interventional procedure). (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2).
3.  **State Law Precedence:** California Insurance Code § 10169.5(a)(2) prohibits conditioning surgical approval on further physical therapy where a member has completed a course of PT and reached a documented functional plateau, which is the case here. (California Regulatory Framework, Part III).
4.  **Clinical Standard Met:** The procedure is consistent with generally accepted standards of medical practice for persistent cervical radiculopathy after an adequate course of conservative treatment has failed to provide sustained relief. (AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines 2023, Section 3.1 Tier 2).

       - Shortfall: There is a literal 1-week shortfall in the duration of supervised physical therapy.

   (b) Pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)): NOT MET
       - Requirement: Trial of at least two specified agents (NSAIDs/COX-2 inhibitors, muscle relaxants, neuropathic agents, or oral corticosteroids) for a minimum of 4 weeks each.
       - Clinical Record: 
         1. Meloxicam (NSAID): 15mg daily for 3 months (compliant).
         2. Prednisone taper (oral corticosteroid): 2 weeks (non-compliant).
       - Shortfall: While the member trialed two appropriate classes of drugs, the second agent (Prednisone) was only trialed for 2 weeks, resulting in a 2-week duration shortfall under the literal 4-week minimum requirement.

   (c) Interventional Treatment (Section 2.2(c)): NOT MET
       - Requirement: At least one interventional treatment, defined as a cervical epidural steroid injection (minimum 1), a cervical medial branch block, or a trigger point injection series.
       - Clinical Record: No interventional treatments have been performed (noted as null).
       - Shortfall: There is a complete shortfall of this requirement, with zero interventional treatments attempted.

3. Section 2.2 — Exception 2.2(A) (Myelopathy Pathway): NOT APPLICABLE
The clinical record was evaluated to determine if the modified conservative treatment requirements under the Myelopathy Pathway apply:
   - Under Exception 2.2(A), the physical therapy requirement is reduced to 4 weeks, and the interventional treatment requirement is waived.
   - However, the "NOTE" in Section 2.2 explicitly states: "The myelopathy exception applies only when myelopathy is the PRIMARY diagnosis. Cases where myelopathy is documented as a finding but radiculopathy is the primary complaint are subject to standard conservative treatment requirements."
   - The member's primary presenting diagnosis is cervical radiculopathy C6-C7. There is no clinical or imaging evidence of cervical myelopathy (no spinal cord compression, no myelomalacia, and no myelopathic symptoms such as gait disturbance, bilateral upper extremity weakness, hyperreflexia, positive Hoffman sign, or bowel/bladder dysfunction).
   - Therefore, the Myelopathy Pathway exception does not apply, and the member remains subject to the standard conservative treatment requirements of Section 2.2.

4. Section 2.3 — Imaging Requirement: MET
The MRI dated 2024-09-01 demonstrates structural pathology (C6-C7 disc herniation and right C7 nerve root compression) consistent with the member's clinical presentation and proposed surgical level. This satisfies Section 2.3.

5. Section 2.4 — Physician Documentation: PARTIALLY MET
The treating physician (Dr. Robert Chen, MD) provided a clinical rationale and declared a functional plateau in the appeal letter. However, under the literal terms of CC-SPINE-2024, a formal plateau is not documented within the physical therapy records themselves, and the literal 6-week duration requirement remains unfulfilled.

IV. SECTION 3 — EXCLUSIONS APPLICABILITY
Under Section 3.2 of CC-SPINE-2024, authorization must be denied if:
"Conservative treatment requirements have not been met as specified in Section 2.2, unless myelopathy exception applies."

Because the member has failed to meet the literal requirements of Section 2.2(a) (5 weeks completed vs. 6 weeks required), Section 2.2(b) (Prednisone trialed for 2 weeks vs. 4 weeks required), and Section 2.2(c) (0 injections vs. 1 required), and because the Myelopathy Pathway exception does not apply, a denial is contractually mandated under Section 3.2.

V. CONCLUSION OF PLAN CRITERIA REVIEW
Under a strict, literal application of HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, the member does not meet the criteria for surgical authorization due to the following specific clinical shortfalls:
1. A 1-week shortfall in supervised physical therapy (Section 2.2(a)).
2. A 2-week duration shortfall in the second pharmacotherapy trial (Section 2.2(b)).
3. A complete absence of required interventional treatment (Section 2.2(c)).

Consequently, under Section 3.2, the prior authorization request for CPT 22551 is non-compliant with the plan's internal medical necessity criteria.
ground_truth_answer: REMAND — The clinical denial may be substantively correct (5 weeks PT vs 6 required, no injection, plateau not formally documented in PT records). However, CHSC 1374.31(b) requires written criteria in the denial notice. Verbal peer-to-peer communication cannot substitute for written notice. Plan must reissue a compliant written denial.
genuine_tension: Clinical criteria not met on the merits — 5 weeks PT, no injection, plateau not formally documented. The denial is substantively defensible. But the procedural violation (criteria communicated verbally only, no IMR notice) independently requires remedy.
